summary: Uniformity for small points and for Mordell–Lang on subvarieties of abelian varieties, extending HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions where its Layer 5 stops (qualitative Mordell–Lang, Bogomolov over number fields, equidistribution). The plan follows Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger’s height inequality for non-degenerate subvarieties, Kühne’s equidistribution in families, Gao–Ge–Kühne’s gap principle, uniform Bogomolov and uniform Mordell–Lang via Rémond’s quantitative Vojta method, the geometric Bogomolov conjecture over function fields (Gao–Habegger in characteristic 0 over curves, Xie–Yuan in general), Yuan’s uniform Bogomolov-type theorem for curves over all global fields with the relative Bogomolov theorem for curve families, and DeMarco–Krieger–Ye’s bielliptic family as a worked case. Betti maps come from AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuliPartII, adelic line bundles, bigness and Moriwaki heights from ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeightsPartII, moduli from PELModuli, StableReductionPartII and JacobianChallengePartII.

nodes.title: Degree of a subvariety with respect to a line bundle
nodes.statement: Let X be a projective scheme over a field k, L a line bundle on X and Z ⊆ X a closed subscheme with irreducible components Z_i of dimension d_i. For an irreducible Z of dimension d put deg_L Z = (c₁(L)^d ∩ [Z]) ∈ ℤ, the degree of the zero-cycle c₁(L)^d ∩ [Z]; for an arbitrary closed Z put deg_L Z = Σ_i deg_L Z_i over all irreducible components (of possibly different dimensions), each counted once with its reduced structure. For L ample, deg_L Z ≥ 1 when Z ≠ ∅. On a product X^M the degree is taken for L^{⊠M} = Σ p_i^*L, and for a closed immersion X ⊆ ℙⁿ it is taken for O(1).
hypotheses: X projective over a field k; L a line bundle on X, ample for the positivity statements.
proofSteps: Define the degree of an irreducible Z through the intersection of c₁(L)^{dim Z} with the fundamental class [Z] in the Chow group of SF.5 and take the degree of the resulting zero-cycle.
Extend to closed subsets by summing over irreducible components with reduced structure; this is the convention of GGK §2 (the total degree), not the degree of the top-dimensional part only.
Positivity for ample L: some multiple of L is very ample, and the degree of Z for the very ample multiple is the projective degree, which is positive; divide by the power of the multiple.

sources.match: Fixes degrees of possibly reducible closed subsets as the sum over irreducible components and records the product and image estimates used throughout.
Uses degrees of subvarieties of projective space and their intersections, with Bézout.

acceptance: A closed point with residue field k has degree 1 for every line bundle; a closed point of residue degree 2 has degree 2.
A line in ℙⁿ has O(1)-degree 1 and a smooth conic has degree 2.
For a curve C of genus g ≥ 1 embedded in its Jacobian by an Abel–Jacobi map, deg_Θ C = g for a theta divisor Θ.

uses.how: exceptional sets X′ are bounded by their total degree
uniform degree bounds for Abel–Jacobi curves in the universal family
deg_{𝔏_g^{⊗4}|A} X = 8^r deg_L X for the principal-polarization normalization

nodes.title: Heights of cycles via Chow forms
nodes.statement: Let n, r, D ≥ 0. For an effective r-dimensional cycle Z of degree D in ℙⁿ over ℚ̄, its Chow form F_Z is a multihomogeneous form, of degree D in each of r + 1 groups of n + 1 variables, determined up to a scalar. The Chow height h_Ch(Z) is the absolute logarithmic Weil height of the coefficient vector of F_Z, i.e. the height of the point [F_Z] of the Chow variety Ch(ℙⁿ, r, D) in its Chow-form embedding. It is comparable with the arithmetic-intersection height h(Z) of the parent (projective cycle height, Fubini–Study metric): the two differ by an amount bounded linearly in D with a constant depending on n and r (Philippon; Bost–Gillet–Soulé).
hypotheses: Z an effective cycle of pure dimension r and degree D in ℙⁿ over ℚ̄.
proofSteps: Construct F_Z from the incidence correspondence of (r+1)-tuples of hyperplanes meeting Z; its coefficients are the Plücker-type coordinates of [Z] in the Chow variety (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.1).
Define h_Ch(Z) as the Weil height of [F_Z] (Mathlib Projectivization.logHeight after descending to a number field of definition and normalizing by its degree).

Compare with the parent’s projective cycle height (HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions RP.5, projective cycle heights with the coefficient-height comparison of the Chow form): the two differ by an amount linear in D. This comparison is Philippon’s (Math. Ann. 289 (1991)) and Bost–Gillet–Soulé’s (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 7 (1994)); neither was read for this plan, and the cited papers only use some such height (gap recorded).

sources.match: Fixes a height function on each Chow variety of cycles of fixed dimension and degree, for instance a Philippon height, without further specification, to measure the subvarieties produced by the bounded-geometry theorem.
Uses the height h(X) of a subvariety of projective space (Bost–Gillet–Soulé) in Rémond’s inequalities.

sources.locator: §6.1, p. 25 and proof of Lemma 6.1, p. 26 (arXiv v3)
sources.match: Uses heights of projective subvarieties and Philippon’s arithmetic Bézout theorem.

acceptance: For a point P ∈ ℙⁿ(ℚ̄) (r = 0, D = 1) the Chow form is the linear form Σ P_i u_i and h_Ch(P) is the Weil height of P.
A coordinate linear subspace has Chow height 0.
Multiplying the defining equations of a hypersurface by a scalar does not change h_Ch: a definition by coefficient vectors before projectivization fails this.

uses.how: the PCF-special subvarieties are bounded in the Chow variety by h_Ch

uses.where: Gao–Ge–Kühne, Lemma A.4 and Theorem A.1

nodes.title: Products of point sets in a proper subvariety (Gao–Ge–Kühne Lemma 4.3)
nodes.statement: Let X be an irreducible projective variety over a field k with a very ample line bundle L, let M ≥ 1 and let Z ⊊ X^M be a proper closed subset. There is c = c(M, dim X, deg_L X, deg_{L^{⊠M}} Z) > 0 such that every subset Σ ⊆ X(k) with Σ^M ⊆ Z(k) lies in X′(k) for a proper closed X′ ⊊ X with deg_L X′ < c.
hypotheses: X irreducible projective over k, L very ample on X; M ≥ 1; Z ⊊ X^M closed; Σ ⊆ X(k) with Σ^M ⊆ Z(k).
proofSteps: Induct on M; for M = 1 take X′ = Z.
Split Z into the union Z′ of components dominating the first factor of X × X^{M−1} and the rest Z″; let q be the first projection.
If the points of Σ outside q(Z″) give a fibre that is a proper subset of X^{M−1}, apply the induction hypothesis to that fibre, whose degree is bounded by Bézout and GGK (2.6).
Otherwise Σ minus q(Z″) lies in a proper fibre X″ × {x}; take X′ = X″ ∪ q(Z″), bounding deg q(Z″) ≤ deg Z″ ≤ deg Z by the image estimate, and enlarge k to an algebraically closed field where needed.

sources.match: States and proves, by induction on M, that a set whose M-th power lies in a proper closed subset lies in a proper closed subset of bounded degree, with the dependence of the bound displayed.
Applies the lemma, for a quasi-projective X with its closure and subvarieties over ℂ, to bound exceptional sets.

acceptance: The bound depends only on M, dim X, deg_L X and deg Z, not on Σ (GGK Lemma 4.3; DMY §5).
For X = ℙ¹, M = 2 and Z the diagonal, any Σ with Σ² ⊆ Δ has at most one point, and X′ may be taken to be that point.
The lemma is stated for all subsets Σ, finite or not: an infinite Σ is forced into X′.

nodes.title: Many points of a curve escape a proper subvariety of its power (DGH Lemma 6.3)
nodes.statement: Let C ⊆ ℙⁿ_k be an irreducible curve over an algebraically closed field and Z ⊆ (ℙⁿ_k)^M a closed subset with C^M ⊄ Z. There is B depending only on M, deg C and deg Z such that every Σ ⊆ C(k) with #Σ ≥ B satisfies Σ^M ⊄ Z(k).
hypotheses: C irreducible curve in ℙⁿ_k, k algebraically closed; Z closed in (ℙⁿ)^M with C^M ⊄ Z.
proofSteps: Apply the product-set lemma to X = C and Z ∩ C^M ⊊ C^M: a Σ with Σ^M ⊆ Z lies in a proper closed subset of C of bounded degree.
A proper closed subset of an irreducible curve is finite with at most its degree many points, so B = c + 1 works with c from the product-set lemma.

sources.match: States that sufficiently many points of a curve have M-th power not contained in a given closed subset not containing C^M, with the bound depending only on M and the degrees, and proves it by induction on M.

acceptance: For M = 1 the statement says a curve not contained in Z meets it in at most deg C · deg Z points (Bézout).
B does not depend on the field of definition of C or on the height of C.

nodes.title: Ball packing in Euclidean space (Rémond)
nodes.statement: Let E be a real Euclidean space of dimension ρ and 0 < r ≤ R. Every subset of a closed ball of radius R in E is covered by at most (1 + 2R/r)^ρ closed balls of radius r centred at points of the subset.
hypotheses: E Euclidean of dimension ρ; 0 < r ≤ R; S ⊆ a closed ball B(x₀, R).
proofSteps: Choose a maximal r-separated subset S₀ ⊆ S; the closed r-balls about S₀ cover S by maximality.
The open balls of radius r/2 about S₀ are disjoint and lie in B(x₀, R + r/2); compare volumes with addHaar_closedBall: #S₀ (r/2)^ρ ≤ (R + r/2)^ρ.
Hence #S₀ ≤ (1 + 2R/r)^ρ.

sources.match: States, as an elementary ball-packing argument, that a subset of a ball of radius R in Γ ⊗ ℝ is covered by at most (1 + 2R/r)^{rk Γ} balls of radius r centred at its elements.
Uses the same covering bound, citing Rémond’s Lemme 6.1, to count points of small height.

acceptance: ρ = 0: one ball suffices, matching (1 + 2R/r)⁰ = 1.
ρ = 1, R = r: an interval of length 2r is covered by three r-balls centred in it, and (1 + 2)¹ = 3.
Centres must lie in the subset: covering by balls with arbitrary centres is the weaker statement, and the counting arguments need centres that are themselves points of the subgroup.

nodes.title: Restricted Hilbert schemes of a polarized abelian variety
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over ℚ̄ with a very ample line bundle L and r, d ≥ 1. Among the finitely many Hilbert polynomials of irreducible r-dimensional subvarieties of L-degree d, the Hilbert schemes of A form a projective scheme H_{r,d}(A) with universal family X_{r,d}(A) ⊆ A × H_{r,d}(A). The locus of points whose fibre is geometrically integral is open; H_{r,d}(A)° is its maximal reduced subscheme. It is a quasi-projective variety whose ℚ̄-points are exactly the irreducible X ⊆ A with dim X = r and deg_L X = d, and for every irreducible component V of H_{r,d}(A) the intersection V ∩ H_{r,d}(A)° is empty or dense open in V.
hypotheses: A abelian over ℚ̄; L very ample; r, d ≥ 1 integers.
proofSteps: Bound the Hilbert polynomials of irreducible subvarieties of fixed dimension and degree (finitely many; AlgebraicModuli R09.1).
Take the disjoint union of the corresponding Hilbert schemes (R09.2) with its universal closed family.
Geometric integrality of fibres of a proper flat family is an open condition; give the open locus its reduced structure.

sources.match: Defines the Hilbert scheme of subvarieties of fixed dimension and degree of a polarized abelian variety, the open locus of geometrically integral fibres and its reduced structure, and states the density property of its intersection with each component.

acceptance: For r = 0 and d = 1 the points are the points of A (the construction is used only for r ≥ 1, but the r = 0 case is A itself).
For r = dim A and d = deg_L A the restricted Hilbert scheme is a single reduced point, the class of A.
In an elliptic surface E × E, the union of two distinct fibres {P} × E and {Q} × E has dimension 1 and degree twice that of a fibre but is not a point of H°: reducible members are excluded.

uses.how: finitely many points of A cut a family of subvarieties down to a finite set
the fibres of the family version over a moduli point are these schemes

nodes.title: The restricted Hilbert scheme over the moduli of principally polarized abelian varieties
nodes.statement: Let π_univ : 𝔄_g → 𝔸_g be the universal principally polarized abelian scheme over the fine moduli space of principally polarized abelian varieties of dimension g with level-4 structure over ℚ̄, and 𝔏_g a symmetric relatively ample line bundle on 𝔄_g/𝔸_g with c₁(𝔏_g|_{A_b}) = 2c₁(L_b) for the principal polarization L_b, so that 𝔏_g^{⊗4} is relatively very ample. For r ≥ 1 and d ≥ 1, H = ⊔_{P∈Ξ} Hilb_P(𝔄_g/𝔸_g) over the finite set Ξ of Hilbert polynomials of r-dimensional subvarieties of 𝔏_g^{⊗4}-degree d is projective over 𝔸_g; the locus with geometrically integral fibre is open, and H° = H_{r,d}(𝔄_g/𝔸_g)° is its maximal reduced subscheme, a quasi-projective ℚ̄-variety with universal family X_{H°} ⊆ A_{H°} = 𝔄_g ×_{𝔸_g} H° → H°. Its ℚ̄-points are the pairs ((A, L), X) with (A, L) principally polarized of dimension g and X ⊆ A irreducible of dimension r and 𝔏_g^{⊗4}-degree d; the fibre of H° → 𝔸_g over b is H_{r,d}(A_b)°.
hypotheses: g ≥ 1, r ≥ 1, d ≥ 1; level-4 structure so that 𝔸_g is a fine moduli scheme.
proofSteps: Import 𝔸_g with its universal abelian scheme from PELModuli M5–M6 (Siegel case, principal polarization, level 4).

Choose 𝔏_g as the symmetric rigidified bundle whose fibres are twice the principal polarization (existence from the polarization theory of AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A2); 𝔏_g^{⊗4} is relatively very ample.
Form the relative Hilbert scheme for the finitely many Hilbert polynomials, restrict to the open locus of geometrically integral fibres and reduce.

sources.match: Introduces the universal abelian variety over the level-4 fine moduli space, the relatively very ample bundle 𝔏_g^{⊗4}, the relative Hilbert scheme with its universal family, the open locus of geometrically integral fibres (the restricted Hilbert scheme) and the fibred-power diagram.

acceptance: For an elliptic curve E (g = 1) and X = E (r = 1), deg_L E = 1 for the principal polarization L = O(0) and deg_{𝔏_1^{⊗4}} E = 8.
For g = 2 and the Abel–Jacobi curve C ⊆ Jac(C) (r = 1), deg_Θ C = 2, so C is a point of H°_{1,16}.
Without level structure the moduli space is only coarse and carries no universal abelian scheme; the construction requires the fine level-4 moduli space.

nodes.title: Fibred powers of the universal subvariety and their moduli maps
nodes.statement: For m ≥ 1 and a morphism S → H° (or S → H_{r,d}(A)°), X_S^{[m]} = X_S ×_S ⋯ ×_S X_S ⊆ A_S^{[m]} = A_S ×_S ⋯ ×_S A_S is the m-fold fibred power, with projection π^{[m]} : X_S^{[m]} → S and moduli map ι^{[m]} : A_S^{[m]} → 𝔄_g^{[m]} to the m-fold fibred power of the universal abelian scheme over 𝔸_g (for a fixed A, the map ι_A^{[m]} to A^m). The fibre over s ∈ S is X_s^m ⊆ A_s^m.
hypotheses: S a variety mapping to H°; m ≥ 1.
proofSteps: Form the fibre products over S of the flat proper universal family; they are flat and proper over S.
The moduli map is the base change of ι_{H°} to the fibred powers.

sources.match: Defines the fibred powers of the universal family over the restricted Hilbert scheme and the commutative diagram of their projections to the base and maps to the fibred powers of the universal abelian scheme.

acceptance: For S a point s, X_S^{[m]} = X_s^m ⊆ A_s^m.
X_S^{[2]} is the fibre product over S, not the absolute product X_S × X_S: for dim S > 0 they have different dimensions (2 dim X_S − dim S versus 2 dim X_S).

uses.how: generic finiteness of ι^{[m]} on X_S^{[m]} and non-degeneracy
the height inequality on X_S^{[m]} forces small points into a degeneracy locus

nodes.title: Finitely many points cut a family of subvarieties to a finite set (GGK Lemmas 3.1–3.2)
nodes.statement: Let V ⊆ H_{r,d}(A)° be a nonempty, possibly reducible subvariety. (1) There are m₀ = m₀(V) points P₁, …, P_{m₀} ∈ A(ℚ̄) such that {[X] ∈ V(ℚ̄) : P₁, …, P_{m₀} ∈ X} is non-empty and finite. (2) Consequently, for every m ≥ m₀ there is P ∈ A^m(ℚ̄) whose fibre under ι_A^{[m]} restricted to X_{r,d}(A)^{[m]} ×_{H} V is non-empty and finite.
hypotheses: A abelian over ℚ̄ with ample L; V ⊆ H_{r,d}(A)° a nonempty subvariety.
proofSteps: Fix X₀ ∈ V. Induct on the dimension of the family of members through the chosen points: in each positive-dimensional component W of the current family choose a point of X₀ not lying on some X_W ≠ X₀; two distinct irreducible subvarieties of the same dimension and degree do not contain one another, so the dimension drops.

At each round choose one such point for every positive-dimensional component of the current parameter locus, keeping X₀ throughout. Each round lowers its maximal positive dimension, so finitely many rounds and finitely many chosen points leave a finite nonempty locus. If it is finite initially, choose one point of X₀ so that m₀ ≥ 1.
For m ≥ m₀ set P = (P₁, …, P_{m₀}, P_{m₀}, …, P_{m₀}); the fibre of ι_A^{[m]} over P projects isomorphically onto the finite set of part (1).

sources.locator: Lemma 3.1 and proof, p. 199; Lemma 3.2 and proof, pp. 199–200
sources.match: Chooses points one at a time inside a fixed member to cut down every positive-dimensional component of the family, then pads the tuple to length m to obtain a finite non-empty fibre of the moduli map.

acceptance: For V a single point the statement holds with m₀ = 1 and any point of X₀.
For V the family of translates of an elliptic curve E × {0} in E × E, one point P₁ = (0, b) cuts V down to the single member E × {b}.

nodes.title: Generic finiteness of the moduli map on fibred powers (GGK Lemma 3.3)
nodes.statement: For an irreducible subvariety S ⊆ H° there is m₀ = m₀(S) ≥ 1 such that ι^{[m]} restricted to X_S^{[m]} is generically finite onto its image for every m ≥ m₀.
hypotheses: S ⊆ H° irreducible.
proofSteps: The fibre of ι^{[m]}|_{X_S^{[m]}} over P ∈ A_b^m equals the fibre computed in GGK (3.8) for V, so by the preceding lemma some fibre is finite and non-empty.
X_S^{[m]} is irreducible (every component dominates S by flatness, and the generic fibre is geometrically irreducible), so upper semicontinuity of fibre dimension gives generic finiteness.

sources.match: Deduces generic finiteness from a finite fibre over one point of a fibre of S → 𝔸_g, using irreducibility of X_S^{[m]} from flatness and geometric irreducibility of the fibres.

acceptance: If S is a point then X_S^{[m]} = X^m maps isomorphically and m₀ = 1.
For S the family of all translates of a fixed X (dim S = g), m₀ grows with the number of points needed to pin a translate.

nodes.title: Non-degenerate fibred powers over the restricted Hilbert scheme (GGK Proposition 3.4)
nodes.statement: Let S ⊆ H° be irreducible with geometric generic point η, and assume (i) X_η is an irreducible subvariety of A_η, (ii) X_s generates A_s for every s ∈ S(ℂ), (iii) X_η has finite stabilizer. Then there is m₀ = m₀(S) ≥ 1 such that X_S^{[m]} is a non-degenerate subvariety of A_S^{[m]} → S for every m ≥ m₀.
hypotheses: S ⊆ H° irreducible satisfying (i)–(iii).
proofSteps: By the generic finiteness lemma, ι^{[m]}|_{X_S^{[m]}} is generically finite for m ≥ m₀(S).
Gao’s non-degeneracy criterion for fibred powers (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuliPartII B4) applies under (i)–(iii) once m ≥ max(m₀, dim S).

sources.match: Combines Gao’s criterion for fibred powers with generic finiteness of the moduli map, replacing m₀ by the maximum of m₀ and dim S.

acceptance: Hypothesis (iii) cannot be dropped: for X_s = A_s (r = g, stabilizer A_s) and dim S > 0, X_S^{[m]} = A_S^{[m]} has complex dimension mg + dim S while its Betti map takes values in a real torus of dimension 2mg, so it is degenerate for every m.
The proposition is applied only to the components of the closure of S_gen (GGK Lemma 3.5), where (i)–(iii) hold.

nodes.title: The locus of finite stabilizer and generation
nodes.statement: For a subvariety S ⊆ H°, S_gen ⊆ S(ℚ̄) is the set of s such that Stab_{A_s}(X_s) is finite and X_s generates A_s (no proper abelian subvariety contains a translate of X_s, equivalently the abelian subvariety generated by X_s − X_s is A_s).
hypotheses: S ⊆ H° a subvariety.
proofSteps: Use the parent’s stabilizers and the abelian subvariety generated by differences.

sources.match: Defines the subset of points of S at which the member has finite stabilizer and generates the abelian variety.

acceptance: For an Abel–Jacobi curve C ⊆ Jac(C) of genus g ≥ 2, the point of H° it defines lies in H°_gen.
For X = B a proper abelian subvariety, Stab(X) = B is infinite and X does not generate A, so [B] ∉ H°_gen.
For X = A, the stabilizer is A, so [A] ∉ H°_gen although A generates A.

uses.how: the gap principle and uniform Bogomolov are proved for s ∈ S_gen
X with positive-dimensional stabilizer has empty X°, so only s ∈ H°_gen matter

nodes.title: Components of the closure of the generic locus satisfy the non-degeneracy hypotheses (GGK Lemma 3.5)
nodes.statement: For a subvariety S ⊆ H°, each irreducible component S′ of the Zariski closure of S_gen, with its reduced structure, satisfies hypotheses (i)–(iii) of the non-degenerate fibred powers theorem for X_{S′} ⊆ A_{S′} → S′.
hypotheses: S ⊆ H° a subvariety; S′ an irreducible component of the closure of S_gen.
proofSteps: (i): every fibre over H° is geometrically integral.

(ii): use the proper difference-sum map X^{[2g]} → A, (x₁,…,x_g,y₁,…,y_g) ↦ Σ(x_i−y_i). Its fibre image equals the abelian subvariety generated by X_s−X_s. Surjectivity holds precisely on the generation locus. The complement of this image in A has open image in S under the smooth structure map, so generation is closed and extends from the dense generic locus.

(iii): if Stab(X_η)⁰ were positive-dimensional, spread it out over a quasi-finite dominant S″ → S′; then every fibre over a dense open has positive-dimensional stabilizer, contradicting density of S_gen.

sources.match: Checks irreducibility from geometric irreducibility of fibres, generation from closedness of the generation condition in proper families, and finiteness of the generic stabilizer by spreading out its identity component.

acceptance: If S_gen is empty there are no components and the statement is vacuous.
The closure is necessary: S_gen itself need not be constructible-open, but its closure’s components carry the hypotheses generically.

nodes.title: The principal polarization and level hypothesis (Hyp)
nodes.statement: An abelian scheme π : A → S over a variety satisfies (Hyp) if it carries a principal polarization and a symplectic level-ℓ structure for some ℓ ≥ 3, compatible with the polarization. Then S → 𝔸_{g,ℓ} classifies it, A is the pullback of the universal abelian scheme, and after shrinking S, A admits a closed immersion A → ℙⁿ × S whose generic fibre is projectively normal, obtained from L^{⊗l}, l ≥ 4, for a symmetric ample L on the generic fibre. Extending the embedding over the base may require a twist by a bundle from S.
hypotheses: π : A → S an abelian scheme over an irreducible quasi-projective variety over ℚ̄; for the embedding, S regular, irreducible, quasi-projective and Zariski open in a projective S̄ ⊆ ℙ^m (DGH §1.2 and Remark 3.1).
proofSteps: A principal polarization and a level-ℓ structure with ℓ ≥ 3 give a classifying map to the fine moduli space (PELModuli M5).

Choose a projectively normal power of a symmetric ample bundle on the generic fibre (A2), choose a basis there, and spread the resulting immersion and equations to a dense open of S. A base twist extends the projective embedding when required; it does not alter fibrewise Néron–Tate heights (DGH Remark 3.1).

sources.match: Introduces the hypothesis that the abelian scheme is principally polarized with level-ℓ structure for some ℓ ≥ 3, used in the body of the paper, and the projectively normal symmetric embedding used for the intersection computations.

acceptance: The Legendre family y² = x(x − 1)(x − λ) over ℙ¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} has full level-2 structure but not level ℓ ≥ 3; adjoining 3-torsion gives a finite étale cover satisfying (Hyp) for g = 1.
A principally polarized abelian variety with level-ℓ structure, ℓ ≥ 3, has no non-trivial automorphism preserving both (Serre’s lemma), which is why the moduli space is fine.
Level 2 does not suffice: [−1] preserves every level-2 structure, so the moduli problem is not rigid.

uses.how: the height inequality is first proved under (Hyp)

uses.where: Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger, Theorem B.1, sixth and seventh dévissages
uses.how: a finite étale base change achieves (Hyp)

nodes.title: The compactly supported cut-off of the Betti form
nodes.statement: Let π : A → S satisfy (Hyp) over ℚ̄ ⊆ ℂ, ω the Betti form on A^an (a closed semipositive (1,1)-form, AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuliPartII B1), s₀ ∈ S^an, Δ a relatively compact contractible neighbourhood of s₀ and ϑ : S^an → [0, 1] smooth with compact support K ⊆ Δ and ϑ(s₀) = 1. Put θ = ϑ ∘ π. Then θω is a smooth semipositive (1,1)-form on A^an with compact support in π^{-1}(K), not closed in general; it extends by zero to the compactification. For a non-degenerate X one takes s₀ = π(P₀) for a smooth point P₀ of X with (ω|_X)^{∧ dim X}_{P₀} > 0.
hypotheses: (Hyp) holds; S^an is the analytification of the smooth locus used to define ω.
proofSteps: On π^{-1}(Δ) the Betti map trivializes A^an as Δ × (ℝ/ℤ)^{2g}, and ω is the pullback of the standard translation-invariant form (B0–B1).
Multiply by θ; semipositivity is pointwise and preserved by multiplication by a nonnegative function; compact support follows from that of ϑ.
Extend by zero, choosing the extension of ϑ to the compactification as recorded in source issue E8 of the DGH extraction (a smooth extension that vanishes off K).

sources.match: Introduces the bump function on the base, the cut-off form θω supported over a compact subset of a contractible neighbourhood, and the choice of base point at a smooth point where the top power of the Betti form is positive.

acceptance: For a constant family A = A₀ × S, ω is the pullback of the flat Kähler form of A₀ (the Betti map is the projection), and θω = ϑ·ω.
θω is not closed when dϑ ≠ 0 on the support of ω: d(θω) = dθ ∧ ω; the proof uses only semipositivity, never closedness of θω.
Pulling back by [2] multiplies θω by 4, matching ĥ([2]P) = 4ĥ(P).

uses.how: the integral of (θω)^d over X_N bounds the self-intersection F^d from below

nodes.title: The graph construction X_N with the line bundles F and M
nodes.statement: Under (Hyp) with A ⊆ ℙⁿ × S ⊆ ℙⁿ × ℙ^m, let X ⊆ A be closed irreducible dominating S and N ≥ 1. Let X_N = {(P, [N]P) : P ∈ X} ⊆ A ×_S A, viewed in ℙⁿ × ℙⁿ × ℙ^m, and X̄_N its Zariski closure, so dim X̄_N = dim X. Put F = O(0, 1, 1)|_{X̄_N} and M = O(0, 0, 1)|_{X̄_N}. For P_N = (P, [N]P) one has h_{X̄_N, F}(P_N) = h([N]P) + O(1) and h_{X̄_N, M}(P_N) = h(π(P)) + O(1), with O(1) depending on N.
hypotheses: (Hyp); X ⊆ A closed irreducible dominating S; N ≥ 1.
proofSteps: The graph of [N] is closed in A ×_S A; restrict to X and close up in the projective triple product.
Heights for O(0,1,1) and O(0,0,1) restricted to X̄_N are, by the height machine (parent RP.0), the Weil heights of the projections up to bounded functions.

sources.match: Defines the graph of multiplication by N restricted to X, its closure in a triple product of projective spaces, and the line bundles F and M whose heights are the naive height of [N]P and of π(P).

acceptance: For N = 1, X̄_1 is the closure of the diagonal copy of X and F restricts to O(1, 1) on X.
For a constant family and X a constant section {P₀} × S with P₀ torsion of order dividing N, X_N lies in {P₀} × {0} × S.
X_N itself is not projective when S is not; intersection numbers are taken on the closure X̄_N.

uses.how: the self-intersection (F^d) and mixed intersection (M·F^{d−1}) on X̄_N are compared, and Siu’s criterion gives sections of F^{⊗q} ⊗ M^{⊗−q c N²}

nodes.title: Lower bound for the top self-intersection (DGH Proposition 4.2)
nodes.statement: Under (Hyp), let X ⊆ A be closed irreducible of dimension d dominating S, with a smooth point of X^an at which (ω|_X)^{∧d} > 0. There is κ > 0, independent of N, such that (F^{·d}) ≥ κ N^{2d} on X̄_N for every N ≥ 1.
hypotheses: (Hyp); X closed irreducible, dim X = d, dominant over S, with a smooth point where the top power of ω|_X is positive.
proofSteps: Choose a Fubini–Study representative α of O(1,1) on A and C > 0 with C·θα − θω ≥ 0 on A_Δ (compactness of K).
Pull back by [N]: C·[N]^*(θα) − N²θω is semipositive, so by the semipositive wedge inequality (C·[N]^*(θα))^{∧d} ≥ N^{2d}(θω)^{∧d} on X ∩ A_Δ.

Integrate over X; the left side is bounded by C^d times the intersection number of F on X̄_N (ComplexComparisonPartII C5, the DGH integration contract), the right side is N^{2d} times a positive constant by the choice of P₀.

sources.match: Proves the N^{2d} lower bound for the self-intersection of F on the graph closure by comparing a Fubini–Study form with the cut-off Betti form, pulling back by [N], and integrating over the graph.

acceptance: For a degenerate X, for instance a constant section of a constant family (d = dim S), the integral of (θω)^d vanishes and no such κ exists.
The exponent is 2d, the total dimension count: the height of [N]P grows like N², and F has d factors.

nodes.title: Upper bound for the mixed intersection (DGH Proposition 4.3)
nodes.statement: With A presented by the projectively normal symmetric embedding of (Hyp) (l ≥ 4) and X ⊆ A closed irreducible of dimension d ≥ 1 dominating S, there is c > 0 depending on the data such that (M·F^{·(d−1)}) ≤ c N^{2(d−1)} on X̄_N for every N a power of 2.
hypotheses: Projectively normal symmetric embedding with l ≥ 4; X dominant over S, dim X = d ≥ 1; N = 2^k.
proofSteps: Write [2^k] by iterating the bihomogeneous quartic formulas for duplication (parent RP.0, duplication by quartics); the coordinates of [N]P are forms of degree 4^k = N² in P with base-dependent coefficients of bounded degree D′.
X̄_N lies in the intersection of hypersurfaces of these degrees; Fulton’s refined Bézout and positivity bound the mixed degree (M·F^{d−1}) by a constant times (4^k max{1, D′})^{d−1}.
Use max{1, D′} in place of D′ in the displayed estimate (4.13) (source issue E9 of the DGH extraction: as printed the bound fails when D′ = 0).

sources.match: Cuts out the graph closure by iterated quartic duplication formulas and bounds the mixed intersection number by Fulton’s positivity, using dominance of X over S but neither (Hyp) nor the Betti form.

acceptance: The exponent 2(d − 1) is one less than in the lower bound, which is what allows Siu’s criterion to produce sections of F^{⊗q} ⊗ M^{⊗ −qcN²}.
For d = 1 the bound says (M) on the curve X̄_N is bounded independently of N, as M is pulled back from the base and X̄_N → π(X) has degree independent of N.

nodes.title: Height inequality on the total space (DGH Proposition 4.1)
nodes.statement: Under (Hyp), let X ⊆ A be closed irreducible of dimension d dominating S, with a smooth point of X^an at which (ω|_X)^{∧d} > 0. There is c₁ > 0 such that for every N a power of 2 there are a Zariski open dense U_N ⊆ X and c₂(N) with h([N]P) ≥ c₁N²h(π(P)) − c₂(N) for all P ∈ U_N(ℚ̄).
hypotheses: (Hyp); X closed irreducible, dimension d, dominant over S; a smooth point with positive top Betti form.
proofSteps: For d ≥ 1 choose a rational c₁ > 0 with c₁ c d < κ, and a positive integer q divisible by its denominator. The case d = 0 is immediate.

The lower and upper intersection bounds imply F^d > d·c₁N²·(M·F^{d−1}). Siu’s nef-difference bound (RP.5) makes F^{⊗q} ⊗ M^{⊗(−qc₁N²)} big. Replacing q by a multiple gives a nonzero section, with all tensor exponents integral.
Heights are bounded below off the base locus of that section (parent RP.0); translate through the graph heights h_F and h_M to get h([N]P) ≥ c₁N²h(π(P)) − c₂(N) on the complement U_N.

sources.match: Deduces the height inequality from the two intersection bounds by Siu’s criterion: a power of F twisted by a negative multiple of M has a non-zero section, and heights are bounded below off its base locus.

acceptance: c₁ does not depend on N; only U_N and c₂ do.

The inequality fails on torsion sections of a non-constant elliptic family over a curve: ĥ = 0 while h(π(P)) is unbounded; such a section is a degenerate subvariety and is excluded by the Betti-form hypothesis.

nodes.title: The height inequality under (Hyp) (DGH Theorem 1.6)
nodes.statement: Let S be a regular irreducible quasi-projective variety over ℚ̄, Zariski open in S̄ ⊆ ℙ^m, and π : A → S an abelian scheme satisfying (Hyp), presented by A → ℙⁿ × S from L^{⊗l}, l ≥ 4, with L symmetric ample on the generic fibre. If X ⊆ A is closed irreducible over ℚ̄, dominates S and is non-degenerate, there are c₁ > 0, c₂ ≥ 0 and a Zariski open dense U ⊆ X with ĥ_A(P) ≥ c₁h(π(P)) − c₂ for all P ∈ U(ℚ̄), where ĥ_A is the fibrewise Néron–Tate height of the embedding bundle.
hypotheses: S regular irreducible quasi-projective over ℚ̄; (Hyp); X closed irreducible, dominant, non-degenerate.
proofSteps: Non-degenerate means full Betti rank somewhere, equivalently (ω|_X)^{∧d} ≠ 0 at a smooth point over S^sm (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuliPartII B1).
Silverman–Tate (parent RP.0): |ĥ(Q) − h(Q)| ≤ c₀ max{1, h(π(Q))}.
Apply the total-space inequality to [N]P and divide by N² = ĥ([N]P)/ĥ(P): ĥ(P) ≥ (c₁ − c₀/N²)h(π(P)) − (c₂(N) + c₀)/N²; fix N a power of 2 with N² ≥ 2c₀/c₁ (killing the Zimmer constant).

sources.match: States the height inequality for non-degenerate dominant subvarieties under (Hyp) and proves it from the total-space inequality and Silverman–Tate, fixing a power of 2 large enough to absorb the Silverman–Tate error.

acceptance: For S a point the statement is trivial (h(π(P)) is constant).
A torsion section of a non-isotrivial elliptic scheme over a curve is degenerate, and on it ĥ = 0 while h(π(P)) is unbounded, so non-degeneracy cannot be dropped.

planet.name: Height inequality under the level hypothesis

nodes.title: DGH height inequality in Weil-height form: comparison with the adelic export
nodes.statement: Let π : A → S be an abelian scheme over an irreducible quasi-projective variety S over ℚ̄, L a symmetric relatively ample line bundle on A/S and M an ample line bundle on a projective compactification S̄ of S. If X ⊆ A is an irreducible (not necessarily closed) non-degenerate subvariety over ℚ̄, there are c₁ > 0, c₂ ≥ 0 and a Zariski open dense U ⊆ X with ĥ_{A,L}(P) ≥ c₁ h_{S̄,M}(π(P)) − c₂ for all P ∈ U(ℚ̄). This is the abelian-scheme Weil-height specialization of AH.5/non-degenerate-height-inequality, compared here with the geometric level-case construction of UB.2; it is not a second owner of the general dynamical inequality.
hypotheses: S irreducible quasi-projective over ℚ̄; L symmetric relatively ample; M ample on a compactification; X irreducible non-degenerate.
proofSteps: Import the general dynamical theorem from AH.5 with f=[2] and its invariant adelic extension. Spread the finitely many data over a number field, identify its fibrewise canonical height with the Néron–Tate height (RP.0), and identify Betti non-degeneracy with adelic non-degeneracy (AH.5). The remaining steps give the geometric comparison route from the level case, not another ownership claim for the general theorem.

Replace X by its closure and S by the closure of π(X) (dévissages 1–2), keeping non-degeneracy by birational invariance of the generic Betti rank (B0); choose the base point over the regular locus as in source issue E15 of the DGH extraction.
Restrict to the regular locus of S (dévissage 3).
Over the function field A is isogenous to a principally polarized abelian variety (Mumford §23); spread the isogeny over a dense open and compare Néron–Tate heights (dévissages 4–5).
Adjoin a level-ℓ structure, ℓ ≥ 3, after a finite étale base change, using quasi-sections (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0) and that heights and non-degeneracy are preserved (dévissage 6).

Apply the (Hyp) case with ĥ_{A,L} comparable to ĥ_A for the embedding bundle (generic independence of fibre heights, parent RP.0), and compare h_{S̄,M} with the restriction of the Weil height (dévissage 7). The count of dévissages and of extra hypotheses follows source issue E5 of the DGH extraction (seven steps; (Hyp) is conditions (v)–(vi)).

sources.locator: Theorem B.1 and proof, pp. 40–47 (arXiv v3)
sources.match: States the height inequality without (Hyp) and without closedness, and reduces it to Theorem 1.6 by successive dévissages: closure, dominance, regular base, isogeny to a principally polarized scheme, principal polarization, level structure after a finite étale base change.
Quotes the height inequality for non-degenerate subvarieties of families over the restricted Hilbert scheme.

acceptance: Theorem B.1 restricted to a curve S and a non-generically-special X recovers Gao–Habegger’s Theorem 1.4 on X* (see the geometric Bogomolov layer).

The Yuan–Zhang height inequality for non-degenerate subvarieties of polarized dynamical systems (ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeightsPartII AH.5) specializes to this statement for A → S with f = [2]; the two proofs are independent (geometric intersection theory here, adelic volumes there).
X need not be closed: a non-degenerate open subset of a closed X gives the same inequality on a smaller U.

nodes.title: The equilibrium measure of a non-degenerate subvariety
nodes.statement: Let π : A → S be a polarized abelian scheme over a smooth irreducible quasi-projective variety over a number field K ⊆ ℂ, and X ⊆ A a non-degenerate irreducible subvariety of dimension d dominating S. The top power (β|_{X^{sm}})^{∧d}, extended by zero, is a nonzero positive Radon measure, where β is Kühne’s semipositive closed form, proportional to the Betti form. The invariant adelic extension supplies its canonical normalization (AH.5). When X admits a generic sequence of height tending to zero, Kühne Theorem 1 and Lemma 25 identify the equidistribution measure as μ_X = κ_X^{-1}(β|_X)^{∧d}, with κ_X the positive finite normalized graph-degree limit. Convergence is against compactly supported tests; this formulation asserts no total mass at the boundary.
hypotheses: A → S abelian scheme over a smooth irreducible base; X ⊆ A irreducible, non-degenerate, dominant.
proofSteps: Restrict the semipositive closed Betti form to the smooth locus of X and take its top power; it is a positive smooth measure on X^{sm}(ℂ), non-zero by non-degeneracy (B1).
Extend by zero across the singular locus (Lelong integration over analytic cycles, ComplexComparisonPartII C5).

Import the canonical measure from AH.5 and its Betti-form comparison. Under the generic-small-sequence hypothesis of Kühne Theorem 1, use Lemma 25 to identify its scalar with κ_X^{-1}; β is proportional to the Betti form by Lemmas 7–8.

sources.locator: Theorem 1, p. 3; Lemmas 7–8, pp. 17–21; Lemma 25, p. 38 (arXiv v4)
sources.match: Constructs, for a non-degenerate subvariety, the limiting measure of Galois orbits of small generic points and identifies it with a multiple of the top exterior power of the Betti form.
Uses that the equilibrium measures of the non-degenerate subvarieties X^{[m(M+2)]} and D(X^{[m(M+2)]}) are proportional to the top powers of the Betti forms.

acceptance: For S a point and X = A, μ_A is a positive multiple of Haar measure on A(ℂ), and the equidistribution theorem specializes to Szpiro–Ullmo–Zhang (whose limit is the normalized Haar measure).
For a torsion section X of an elliptic scheme over a curve, (ω|_X) vanishes identically, X is degenerate and no equilibrium measure is defined.
For a non-torsion section of a non-isotrivial elliptic scheme over a curve (DeMarco–Mavraki), the measure is the pullback of the flat form by the section, a positive measure on the base curve.

uses.how: the measures μ₁ on X^{[m(M+2)]} and the pullback of μ₂ on its difference image are shown not proportional
the limit of Galois orbits of small generic sequences

On a non-degenerate product subvariety of dimension e, its equilibrium measure is the e-th power of this restricted form with the canonical scalar. This does not assert an unspecified product measure on S.

nodes.title: Equidistribution in families of abelian varieties (Kühne)
nodes.statement: Let π : A → S be an abelian scheme over a smooth irreducible quasi-projective variety over a number field, L a symmetric relatively ample line bundle and X ⊆ A a non-degenerate irreducible subvariety dominating S, with equilibrium measure μ_X at an archimedean place. For every continuous compactly supported f on X(ℂ) and every ε > 0 there are δ > 0 and a proper Zariski closed Z ⊊ X such that |∫ f dμ_X − (1/#O(x)) Σ_{y ∈ O(x)} f(y)| < ε for every x ∈ (X ∖ Z)(ℚ̄) with ĥ_L(x) < δ, where O(x) is the Galois orbit of x. Equivalently, the Galois orbits of every X-generic sequence (x_i) with ĥ_L(x_i) → 0 converge weakly to μ_X on compactly supported test functions.
hypotheses: S smooth irreducible quasi-projective over a number field; X non-degenerate irreducible dominant; test functions continuous with compact support.
proofSteps: Generic-sequence form: by the Yuan–Zhang theorem for non-degenerate subvarieties of the polarized dynamical system (A, [2], L) (ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeightsPartII AH.5, part (2)), Galois orbits of a generic sequence with ĥ_L → 0 equidistribute for the canonical measure of L̄_{[2]}|_X.

Identify the canonical measure with μ_X at archimedean places (BettiEquilibriumMeasure.compare_canonical): the curvature form of the invariant metric on L is the Betti form (Kühne Lemma 25; Yuan–Zhang §6.2.2).

Uniform form: if no (δ, Z) existed for some f, ε, choose x_i with ĥ(x_i) < 1/i avoiding the first i members of an enumeration of proper closed subsets defined over the number field and violating the estimate; this sequence is generic, contradicting the generic form.

Kühne’s own proof (DGH height inequality, arithmetic intersection on compactified models, a family version of Zhang’s variational argument) is an alternative route that avoids adelic line bundles on quasi-projective varieties.

sources.match: Proves that Galois orbits of small generic sequences on a non-degenerate subvariety of a family of abelian varieties equidistribute to a measure on compactly supported continuous test functions.
Uses the theorem in the uniform form with δ and an exceptional proper closed subset, citing Kühne Theorem 1 and noting that Yuan–Zhang Theorem 6.7 and Gauthier give it too.

acceptance: For S a point and X=A, this is Szpiro–Ullmo–Zhang equidistribution with Haar probability measure (parent RP.5). For a general X the canonical measure is the normalized restricted curvature power, not ambient Haar measure.
Compact support of f is necessary: mass of Galois orbits may escape to the boundary of S, so test functions on the non-compact X(ℂ) must have compact support.
Non-degeneracy is necessary: a torsion section of an elliptic scheme over a curve has ĥ = 0 at every point and Galois orbits of its points accumulate according to the base, not to a Betti measure.

nodes.title: Uniform Bogomolov over the restricted Hilbert scheme (GGK Proposition 5.2)
nodes.statement: Let S ⊆ H° = H°_{r,d}(𝔄_g/𝔸_g) be a subvariety over ℚ̄ and 𝓛 = ι^*𝔏_g^{⊗4}. There are c″₂, c″₃ > 0 depending on r, d and S such that for every s ∈ S_gen the set {x ∈ X_s°(ℚ̄) : ĥ_𝓛(x) ≤ c″₃} lies in a proper Zariski closed X′ ⊊ X_s with deg_{𝓛_s} X′ < c″₂.
hypotheses: S ⊆ H° a subvariety over ℚ̄; s ranges over S_gen.
proofSteps: Induct on dim S; decompose into irreducible components and pass to the components S′ of the closure of S_gen, which satisfy the non-degeneracy hypotheses.

Step 1: choose m with X_{S′}^{[m]} non-degenerate and M with the generic fibre of the difference map D₀ on X^{m(M+1)} an orbit of the finite stabilizer (Zhang’s difference lemma, parent RP.5); X^{[m(M+2)]} and its image under D = (id, D₀) are non-degenerate (B4 difference product).

Step 2: with μ₁ the equilibrium measure of X^{[m(M+2)]} and μ₂ that of its D-image, D^*μ₂ vanishes at a diagonal point (z, Δ_z) where μ₁ does not (the differential of D has a kernel there), so μ₁ and ν = (1/d_D) D^*μ₂ are not proportional on the finite étale locus of D (source issue E17 of the GGK extraction: compare μ₁ with ν, keep μ₂ in its original normalization).
Step 3: choose f₁ compactly supported in the étale locus separating μ₁ from ν; average over the stabilizer group so that f₁ = f₂ ∘ D.

Step 4: by family equidistribution applied to both subvarieties, every point x of X^{[m(M+2)]} outside a proper closed subset has ĥ(x) ≥ δ or ĥ(D(x)) ≥ δ; use small-height hypotheses in both orbit estimates (source issue E16) and keep the ≥ alternative.

Step 5: if many small points of X_s° existed, their m(M+2)-fold products would land in the exceptional closed subset; the product-set lemma bounds the resulting proper X′ ⊊ X_s in degree, and the induction hypothesis handles the lower-dimensional strata of S. The block indices and degree normalizations follow source issues E6–E7.

sources.match: Runs a family version of the Ullmo–Zhang argument: non-degenerate fibred powers and their difference images, two equilibrium measures shown not to be proportional, a test function constant on fibres of the difference map, a uniform small-height alternative, and noetherian induction with the product-set lemma.

acceptance: For dim S = 0 the first three steps are the Ullmo–Zhang proof of the Bogomolov conjecture for one abelian variety (parent RP.5).
The stabilizer is only assumed finite, not trivial: the averaging of Step 3 over the stabilizer is what handles it.
The constants depend on S, r and d, not on s.

nodes.title: Uniform Bogomolov with an exceptional set (GGK Proposition 5.1)
nodes.statement: For positive integers g, l, r, d there are c″₂, c″₃ > 0 depending on g, l, r, d such that for every polarized abelian variety (A, L) over ℚ̄ of dimension g with deg_L A = l and every irreducible X ⊆ A generating A with dim X = r and deg_L X = d, the set {x ∈ X°(ℚ̄) : ĥ_{L⊗[−1]^*L}(x) ≤ c″₃} lies in a proper Zariski closed X′ ⊊ X with deg_L X′ < c″₂.
hypotheses: (A, L) polarized over ℚ̄, dim A = g, deg_L A = l; X irreducible generating A, dim X = r, deg_L X = d.
proofSteps: Principal case: apply the family version with S = H°_{r, 8^r d}, the degree normalization deg_{𝔏_g^{⊗4}|A} X = 8^r d and ĥ_{𝔏_g^{⊗4}|A} = 4ĥ_{L⊗[−1]^*L} (GGK (4.10), (4.12)); if Stab(X) is positive-dimensional then X° = ∅.

General polarizations: pass to a principally polarized isogenous (A₀, L₀) through the isogeny u₀ and its quasi-inverse u, rescaling c″₃ by (l/g!)² and the degree bound c″₂ by (l/g!)^{2(r−1)}, exactly as in the deduction of the gap principle for all polarizations (source issue E4 of the GGK extraction records the needed rescaling of the degree constant).

sources.match: States the uniform Bogomolov bound with an exceptional proper closed subset of bounded degree for arbitrary polarizations and deduces it from the restricted-Hilbert-scheme version as the gap-principle propositions are deduced.

acceptance: The constants do not depend on A, only on g, l, r, d.
If X does not generate A the statement is applied to X − P inside the abelian subvariety it generates; generation is a hypothesis here, removed in the uniform Bogomolov theorem.

nodes.title: The uniform Bogomolov theorem (Gao–Ge–Kühne Theorem 1.3)
nodes.statement: For positive integers g and d there are c₃ = c₃(g, d) > 0 and c₄ = c₄(g, d) > 0 such that for every polarized abelian variety (A, L) over ℚ̄ of dimension at most g and every irreducible closed X ⊆ A with deg_L X ≤ d (generating A or not), #{P ∈ X°(ℚ̄) : ĥ_{L⊗[−1]^*L}(P) ≤ c₃} < c₄. In the generating case this is GGK Theorem 1.3 as printed; the statement for all X is the form its proof in §8 needs.
hypotheses: (A, L) polarized over ℚ̄ with dim A ≤ g; X ⊆ A irreducible closed with deg_L X ≤ d.
proofSteps: Induct on dim X, with the zero-dimensional case bounded by one point. If the small-point set in X° is empty there is nothing to count; otherwise choose P₀ in that set and set B = ⟨X−X⟩, Y = X−P₀ ⊆ B. Then Y generates B and deg_{L|B} B is bounded in terms of g,d by the parent’s generated-subvariety bound.

Apply the exceptional-set theorem to Y ⊆ B. For the symmetric height, ĥ(P−P₀) ≤ 2ĥ(P)+2ĥ(P₀); choosing the final threshold at most one quarter of the exceptional threshold places every original small point into P₀+Y′. Take minima and maxima over the finitely many bounded dimensions and integral degrees involved.

The components of P₀+Y′ have smaller dimension and bounded total degree. Apply induction in the original ambient polarized A to each component. A point of X° in a component lies in that component’s Ueno complement, because every positive-dimensional coset in the component also lies in X. Sum the bounds and enlarge c₄ to make the final inequality strict.
This repairs both the initial non-generating case and the non-generating exceptional components. In the generating case it recovers GGK Theorem 1.3, whose second constant is c₄ (E1).

sources.match: Theorem 1.3 assumes that X generates A. The node proves its extension to arbitrary irreducible X by the translated, rescaled induction explained in its proof; §8 requires the same stronger induction for exceptional components.
Proves the case of curves embedded in their Jacobians with level structure.

acceptance: For X a curve of genus ≥ 2 in its Jacobian (X° = X), the theorem bounds the number of points of height ≤ c₃ uniformly in the curve: this is Kühne’s uniform Bogomolov for curves.
X° cannot be replaced by X: a positive-dimensional coset contains infinitely many torsion points.
The bound c₃ is absolute (not scaled by h_Fal(A)); the gap principle is the companion statement with a threshold proportional to max{1, h_Fal(A)}.

nodes.title: Uniform Manin–Mumford for curves (Kühne Theorem 2)
nodes.statement: For each g ≥ 2 there is c(g) ≥ 1 such that for every smooth projective curve C of genus g over ℂ (Kühne Theorem 2), and more generally over any algebraically closed field F of characteristic 0, and every divisor D of degree 1 on C, #(ι_D(C) ∩ Jac(C)_tors) ≤ c(g), where ι_D(q) = [q] − D. This implies Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger Theorem 1.4 — #((C(ℚ̄) − P₀) ∩ Jac(C)_tors) ≤ c(g, d) for curves over number fields of degree ≤ d and P₀ ∈ C(ℚ̄) — with a constant independent of d.
hypotheses: g ≥ 2; C smooth projective of genus g over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0; D of degree 1.
proofSteps: Over ℚ̄: X = ι_D(C) ⊆ J = Jac(C) is a curve of degree g for the theta polarization, generating J, with X° = X since a curve of genus ≥ 2 contains no positive-dimensional coset.
Torsion points have Néron–Tate height 0 ≤ c₃, so the uniform Bogomolov theorem with (g, d) = (g, g) bounds their number by c₄(g, g).

Over an arbitrary algebraically closed F of characteristic 0: the torsion points of ι_D(C) are defined over a finitely generated field; specialize to ℚ̄ along a model keeping the curve smooth and the finitely many torsion points distinct (torsion injects under specialization in characteristic 0), as in the specialization step of the uniform Mordell–Lang layer.

This also proves DGH Theorem 1.4 with a constant independent of d (DGH’s own constant depends on d), and gives the bound uniform in P₀ that the small-height step of its printed proof lacks (E6). Kühne states Theorem 2 over ℂ; the step over arbitrary F is the specialization argument above (Kühne Theorem 4 with Γ the torsion subgroup gives the same).

For extension from ℚ̄ to an arbitrary algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, spread any finite configuration of torsion points with the curve and preserve distinctness and their finite orders on a suitable fibre. A putative violation of the uniform bound has such a finite witness; it is unnecessary to define all torsion points over one finitely generated field.

sources.match: States the uniform bound, depending only on the genus, for torsion points on a curve embedded in its Jacobian by a degree-one divisor.
Records that the threshold-zero case of the new gap principle is a uniform Manin–Mumford theorem for curves, and that DeMarco–Krieger–Ye had treated a family of genus-two curves.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.4, p. 3 and its proof p. 36 (arXiv v3)
sources.match: States uniform Manin–Mumford for curves of bounded field degree, with a constant depending on the genus and the degree; the small-height case of its proof needs a bound uniform in the base point (source issue E6 of the DGH extraction).

acceptance: Stoll’s bielliptic genus-2 curve y² = x⁶ + 130x³ + 13 with a Weierstrass base point has 34 torsion points on its image, so c(2) ≥ 34 (DeMarco–Krieger–Ye Remark 1.2).
No uniform bound on the order of these torsion points exists (DeMarco–Krieger–Ye Proposition 9.2 of the published version).
For g = 1 the statement is false: every point of an elliptic curve is the image of a degree-one divisor class, and torsion is infinite.

nodes.title: Uniform degree and height of Abel–Jacobi curves (DGH Lemma 6.1)
nodes.statement: Fix g ≥ 2, a level ℓ ≥ 3, the fine moduli space M_g of smooth genus-g curves with level-ℓ structure over ℚ̄ with universal curve C_g, the Torelli map τ : M_g → A_g to the fine Siegel moduli space with universal abelian scheme 𝔄_g ⊆ ℙⁿ × A_g, and an ample M on a compactification of A_g. There is c such that for all s ∈ M_g(ℚ̄): (i) deg(C_s − P) ≤ c for every P ∈ 𝔄_{g,τ(s)}(ℚ̄); (ii) some P_s ∈ C_s(ℚ̄) satisfies h(C_s − P_s) ≤ c·max{1, h_{A_g,M}(τ(s))}, where h is the height of a subvariety of ℙⁿ.
hypotheses: g ≥ 2; level ℓ ≥ 3; fine moduli; projective immersion of the universal abelian scheme; M ample on a compactification.
proofSteps: The curves C_s − P, s ∈ M_g, P ∈ 𝔄_{g,τ(s)}, form one algebraic family over 𝔄_g ×_{A_g} M_g; degrees of fibres of a family are bounded (constructibility and Bézout), giving (i).

Choose an étale quasi-section of C_g → M_g (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0, EGA IV 17.16.3(ii)); over each piece of a finite stratification the point P_s is given by a morphism, so its height is ≤ c max{1, h(τ(s))} by the height machine.

C_s − P_s is a component of an intersection of the universal family with fixed hypersurfaces through the moduli point; arithmetic Bézout (parent RP.5, projective cycle heights) bounds its height linearly in the height of the point.

sources.match: Proves the uniform degree bound for translates of the curves in the universal Jacobian and a linear bound in the moduli height for the height of a suitable translate, by a quasi-section of the universal curve, constructibility of images, Bézout and Philippon’s arithmetic Bézout theorem.

acceptance: The constant does not depend on s; only (ii) depends on the moduli height.
For P arbitrary the height of C_s − P can be arbitrarily large (translate by points of large height), so (ii) chooses P_s.

nodes.title: Few base points force a proper subvariety (DGH Lemma 6.4)
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over ℚ̄, C ⊆ A a smooth curve of genus g ≥ 2, M ≥ 1, D_M : C^{M+1} → A^M the Faltings–Zhang map (P₀, …, P_M) ↦ (P₁ − P₀, …, P_M − P₀) and Z ⊊ D_M(C^{M+1}) an irreducible proper closed subset. Then #{P ∈ C(ℚ̄) : (C − P)^M ⊆ Z} ≤ 84(g − 1).
hypotheses: C ⊆ A smooth curve of genus g ≥ 2; Z ⊊ D_M(C^{M+1}) irreducible proper closed.
proofSteps: The proper image D_M(C^{M+1}) is irreducible of dimension at most M+1. Thus its proper irreducible subset Z has dimension at most M. If any (C−P)^M lies in Z, both have dimension M and are equal. There is no case dim Z > M.
Then C − P₀ = C − P₁, so P₁ − P₀ stabilizes C − P₀, and translation by it is an automorphism of the curve.
The stabilizer of a genus-≥ 2 curve is finite and embeds in Aut(C), of order at most 84(g − 1) (Hurwitz).

sources.match: Shows that two base points with (C − P)^M in the same irreducible proper closed subset differ by a point stabilizing a translate of C, which acts as an automorphism, and concludes with the Hurwitz bound.

acceptance: The bound is independent of A, M and Z.
For an elliptic curve (g = 1) every point stabilizes C − P and the lemma fails; genus ≥ 2 is used through finiteness of the stabilizer.

nodes.title: Néron–Tate distance between points on curves (DGH Proposition 7.1)
nodes.statement: With M_g, τ, 𝔄_g and M as in the Abel–Jacobi bounds, for each irreducible closed S ⊆ M_g over ℚ̄ there are c₁, c₂, c₃, c₄ > 0 such that for every s ∈ S(ℚ̄) with h_{A_g,M}(τ(s)) ≥ c₁ there is a set Ξ_s ⊆ C_s(ℚ̄) with #Ξ_s ≤ c₂ such that every P ∈ C_s(ℚ̄) satisfies either P ∈ Ξ_s or #{Q ∈ C_s(ℚ̄) : ĥ(Q − P) ≤ h_{A_g,M}(τ(s))/c₃} < c₄.
hypotheses: S ⊆ M_g irreducible closed; s with large modular height.
proofSteps: Induct on dim S. Gao’s theorem (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuliPartII B4, DGH Theorem 6.2) makes D_M(C_S^{[M+1]}) non-degenerate for M = 3g − 2; the height inequality gives c > 0 and a proper closed exceptional set Z_S with Σ ĥ(P_i − P₀) ≥ c h(τ(s)) − c′ off Z_S.

If (C_s − P)^M ⊄ Z_s, at least one of M points close to P escapes Z_s once there are c₄ such points (the escape lemma); the inequality then forces ĥ(Q − P) > h(τ(s))/c₃ with c₃ = 2M/c for one of them.

The base points P with (C_s − P)^M ⊆ Z_s number at most 84(g − 1) per component (the base-point bound): they form Ξ_s, of bounded size; the lower-dimensional part of Z_S over a proper closed subset of S is handled by induction.

sources.match: Proves by induction on dim S that, for curves of large modular height, outside a bounded exceptional set of base points few points are close in Néron–Tate distance, from Gao’s non-degeneracy of D_M(C_S^{[M+1]}) with M = 3g − 2 and the height inequality.

acceptance: The threshold h/c₃ grows with the modular height, unlike the uniform Bogomolov threshold, which is absolute.
Below the modular height bound c₁ the proposition says nothing; the uniform Bogomolov theorem covers that range.

nodes.title: Height gap on the restricted Hilbert scheme (GGK Proposition 4.2)
nodes.statement: Let S ⊆ H° be a subvariety over ℚ̄, 𝓛 = ι^*𝔏_g^{⊗4} and M the pullback to H° of an ample line bundle on a compactification of 𝔸_g. There are c′₁, c′₂, c′₃ > 0 depending on r, d and S such that for each s ∈ S_gen the set {x ∈ X_s°(ℚ̄) : ĥ_𝓛(x) ≤ c′₁ max{1, h_{H°,M}(s)} − c′₃} lies in a proper Zariski closed X′ ⊊ X_s with deg_{𝓛_s} X′ < c′₂.
hypotheses: S ⊆ H° a subvariety; M pulled back from an ample moduli bundle; s ∈ S_gen.
proofSteps: Reduce to S irreducible and to the components S′ of the closure of S_gen; take m with X_{S′}^{[m]} non-degenerate.

Apply UB.2 with an ample height on a compactification of S′. The height of its moduli image is bounded above by a positive multiple of this height plus a constant (height machine for the moduli morphism). Hence Σ ĥ_𝓛(x_i) ≥ c·h_M(s)−c′ off a proper closed Z; no ampleness of the pulled-back M on H° is used.
Case (i): the points s over which Z contains the whole fibre form a proper closed subset of S′; its components are handled by the induction hypothesis.

Case (ii): otherwise Z_s ⊊ X_s^m, and points of height ≤ (c/m)h_M(s) − c′/m have m-th power in Z_s; the product-set lemma gives X′ of bounded degree, the bound depending on deg Z_s, which is uniform over the family.

sources.match: Proves the family gap principle by noetherian induction on dim S: on the generic part the height inequality on a non-degenerate fibred power forces the small points into a degeneracy locus, and the product-set lemma bounds the resulting exceptional set.

acceptance: The base case dim S = 0 is trivial: h_M(s) is constant, and the set of points of height below a constant minus c′₃ can be made empty.
The degree bound of X′ depends on S only through the family, not on s.

nodes.title: Height gap for principally polarized abelian varieties (GGK Proposition 4.4)
nodes.statement: For positive integers g, r, d there are c′₁, c′₂, c′₃ > 0 depending on g, r, d such that for every principally polarized (A, L) over ℚ̄ of dimension g and every irreducible X ⊆ A generating A with dim X = r and deg_L X = d, the set {x ∈ X°(ℚ̄) : ĥ_{L⊗[−1]^*L}(x) ≤ c′₁ max{1, h_Fal(A)} − c′₃} lies in a proper Zariski closed X′ ⊊ X with deg_L X′ < c′₂.
hypotheses: (A, L) principally polarized over ℚ̄ of dimension g; X irreducible generating A with dim r, degree d.
proofSteps: If Stab(X) is positive-dimensional, X° = ∅; otherwise [X] ∈ H°_gen for H° = H°_{r, 8^r d}.
Apply the family gap with S = H°: deg_{𝔏_g^{⊗4}|A} X = 8^r d and ĥ_{𝔏_g^{⊗4}|A} = 4ĥ_{L⊗[−1]^*L}.

Faltings’ comparison of the moduli height with the stable Faltings height (ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights R35.5, GGK (4.11)): max{1, h_Fal(A)} ≤ c(g)h_M(b) + c′(g) log(h_M(b) + 2); rescale c′₁ and c′₃.
deg_L X′ ≤ deg_{𝔏_g^{⊗4}|A} X′ < c′₂ (source issue E3 of the GGK extraction: the inequality is not strict for zero-dimensional components, which does not affect the bound).

sources.match: Specializes the family gap principle to S = H°_{r, 8^r d}, converts degrees and heights between L and 𝔏_g^{⊗4}, and replaces the moduli height by the Faltings height using Faltings’ comparison.

acceptance: The constants depend only on g, r, d; the exceptional set X′ depends on A and X but has bounded degree.
h_Fal is the stable Faltings height in the normalization of ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights R35.3.

nodes.title: Height gap for all polarizations (GGK Proposition 4.1)
nodes.statement: For positive integers g, l, r ≤ g and d there are c′₁, c′₂, c′₃ > 0 depending on g, l, r, d such that for every polarized (A, L) over ℚ̄ of dimension g with deg_L A = l and every irreducible X ⊆ A generating A with dim X = r and deg_L X = d, the set {x ∈ X°(ℚ̄) : ĥ_{L⊗[−1]^*L}(x) ≤ c′₁ max{1, h_Fal(A)} − c′₃} lies in a proper Zariski closed X′ ⊊ X with deg_L X′ < c′₂.
hypotheses: (A, L) polarized over ℚ̄, dim g, deg_L A = l; X irreducible generating A.
proofSteps: Put n = l/g!. Choose a principally polarized (A₀,L₀) and isogenies u₀ : A → A₀ and u : A₀ → A with u∘u₀ = [n], u₀∘u = [n], u₀^*L₀ algebraically equivalent to L, and u^*L algebraically equivalent to [n]^*L₀ (GGK Lemma 2.2(iv)).
Apply the principal case to X₀ = u^{-1}(X)-component; h_Fal(A₀) and h_Fal(A) differ by O(log l) (isogeny estimate, ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights R35.4).

Transport X′₀ to X′ = u(X′₀); by the projection formula deg_L X′ ≤ deg_{u^*L} X′₀ ≤ (l/g!)^{2(r−1)} c′₂, so c′₂ must be rescaled by (l/g!)^{2(r−1)} as well as c′₁ by (l/g!)² (source issue E4 of the GGK extraction).

sources.match: Reduces an arbitrary polarization of degree l to a principal one through an isogeny u₀ and a quasi-inverse u, using the projection formula and Faltings’ isogeny estimate.

acceptance: For l = g! (principal polarization) the statement is the principal case.
The degree constant genuinely changes under the reduction; a proof that keeps c′₂ fixed is wrong (E4).

nodes.title: The gap principle for fixed polarization degree and dimension (GGK Proposition 6.1)
nodes.statement: For positive integers g, l, r, d there are c₁, c₂ > 0 depending on g, l, r, d such that for every polarized (A, L) over ℚ̄ of dimension g with deg_L A = l and every irreducible X ⊆ A generating A with dim X = r and deg_L X = d, the set {P ∈ X°(ℚ̄) : ĥ_{L⊗[−1]^*L}(P) ≤ c₁ max{1, h_Fal(A)}} lies in a proper Zariski closed X′ ⊊ X with deg_L X′ < c₂.
hypotheses: (A, L), X as in the polarized height gap.
proofSteps: Let c′₁, c′₂, c′₃ be the height-gap constants and c″₂, c″₃ the uniform Bogomolov constants; put H = max{1, h_Fal(A)} and B = max{1, 2c′₃/c′₁}.
If H > B, then c′₁H − c′₃ ≥ (c′₁/2)H, so with c₁ ≤ c′₁/2 the height-gap exceptional set works.
If H ≤ B, then c₁H ≤ c₁B ≤ c″₃ for c₁ ≤ c″₃/B, so the uniform Bogomolov exceptional set works.

For fixed A only one of the two cases occurs, so a single exceptional set suffices and c₂ = max{c′₂, c″₂} as published (the extraction’s historical E8 is retracted: no union of exceptional sets is needed).

sources.match: Combines the height gap (threshold proportional to the Faltings height minus a constant) with the uniform Bogomolov exceptional-set version (absolute threshold) to remove the additive constant.

acceptance: The threshold is now c₁ max{1, h_Fal(A)} with no subtracted constant.
c₂ is max{c′₂, c″₂}, not their sum.

nodes.title: The new gap principle (Gao–Ge–Kühne Theorem 1.2)
nodes.statement: Given positive integers g and d there are c₁ = c₁(g, d) > 0 and c₂ = c₂(g, d) > 0 such that for every polarized abelian variety (A, L) over ℚ̄ of dimension g and every irreducible closed X ⊆ A generating A with deg_L X ≤ d, the set {P ∈ X°(ℚ̄) : ĥ_{L⊗[−1]^*L}(P) ≤ c₁ max{1, h_Fal(A)}} is contained in X′(ℚ̄) for a proper Zariski closed X′ ⊊ X with deg_L X′ < c₂.
hypotheses: (A, L) polarized over ℚ̄, dim A = g; X irreducible closed generating A, deg_L X ≤ d.
proofSteps: Since X generates A, deg_L A is bounded in terms of g and deg_L X (GGK Lemma 2.5, via the generated abelian subvariety of the parent and the sum-of-translates degree bound; source issue E2 of the GGK extraction corrects its constants).
Apply the fixed-degree gap principle for each of the finitely many (l, r, d′) with l bounded, r ≤ g, d′ ≤ d; take the minimum of the c₁ and the maximum of the c₂.

sources.match: States the gap principle with threshold proportional to the Faltings height and exceptional set of bounded degree, and deduces it from the fixed-degree version since l = deg_L A is bounded in terms of g and d for generating X.

acceptance: The generation hypothesis cannot be dropped, and the exceptional set is not finite in general (examples in Gao’s survey §10.2 cited by GGK p. 192).
For a curve of genus g ≥ 2 embedded in its Jacobian, X′ is a finite set of bounded cardinality: this is the gap principle for curves.

nodes.title: The new gap principle for curves
nodes.statement: For each g ≥ 2 there are c₁(g), c₂(g) > 0 such that for every smooth projective curve C of genus g over ℚ̄ and every y ∈ C(ℚ̄), #{x ∈ C(ℚ̄) : ĥ(x − y) ≤ c₁ max{h_Fal(C), 1}} ≤ c₂, where h_Fal(C) = h_Fal(Jac(C)) is the stable Faltings height and ĥ is half the canonical height of the symmetric twice-theta bundle (the Néron–Tate height for the principal polarization).
hypotheses: g ≥ 2; C smooth projective genus g over ℚ̄; y ∈ C(ℚ̄).
proofSteps: X = C − y ⊆ J = Jac(C) is a curve of θ-degree g generating J with X° = X.
Apply the new gap principle with (g, d) = (g, g): the small points lie in a proper closed subset of X of degree < c₂, i.e. a finite set of fewer than c₂ points.
With L the symmetric principal polarization, ĥ_{L⊗[−1]^*L} = 2ĥ_L, and 2ĥ_L is the canonical height of the twice-theta bundle; absorb the factor into c₁.

sources.match: States the gap principle for curves with threshold proportional to max{h_Fal(C), 1}, attributing it to Gao’s survey Theorem 4.1 as a combination of DGH Proposition 7.1 and Kühne Theorem 3.
The general gap principle, whose case X = C − y ⊆ Jac(C) gives this statement.

acceptance: Taking the threshold 0 recovers uniform Manin–Mumford for curves.
Yuan’s uniform Bogomolov for curves (the last layer) strengthens this by adding ĥ((2g − 2)α − ω) to the threshold and allowing α ∈ Pic¹ and all global fields.

nodes.title: The Néron–Tate Euclidean space of a finite-rank subgroup
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over ℚ̄ with a symmetric ample line bundle L and Γ ⊆ A(ℚ̄) a subgroup of finite rank ρ. On Γ_ℝ = (Γ/Γ_tors) ⊗ ℝ the Néron–Tate height extends to a positive definite quadratic form; write |P| = ĥ_L(P)^{1/2} and ⟨P, Q⟩ = (ĥ_L(P + Q) − ĥ_L(P) − ĥ_L(Q))/2. Then (Γ_ℝ, ⟨·,·⟩) is a Euclidean space of dimension ρ, the image of Γ in it is a subgroup whose rational span has dimension ρ (dense when Γ is a division group), and points of Γ with equal image differ by torsion.
hypotheses: A abelian over ℚ̄; L symmetric ample; Γ ⊆ A(ℚ̄) of finite rank ρ.
proofSteps: The Néron–Tate pairing (parent RP.0) is symmetric bilinear on A(ℚ̄) and vanishes exactly on torsion when paired with itself (Néron–Tate kernel over number fields).

Choose a finitely generated Γ₀ ⊆ Γ of rank ρ defined over a number field; ĥ is positive definite on Γ₀ ⊗ ℝ (finitely generated Mordell–Weil lattice), and Γ ⊆ division hull of Γ₀ (parent RP.5 finite rank), so Γ_ℝ = Γ₀ ⊗ ℝ.

sources.match: Endows Γ ⊗ ℝ with the Euclidean norm given by the square root of the Néron–Tate height and covers it by cones of small angle.
Works in the Euclidean space Γ ⊗ ℝ with the Néron–Tate norm for the ball-packing count.

acceptance: For Γ = A_tors, Γ_ℝ = 0.
For E: y² = x³ − 2 over ℚ and Γ = E(ℚ) = ℤ·(3, 5), Γ_ℝ ≅ ℝ with |(3,5)|² = ĥ((3,5)) (native Tau Ceti canonical height divided by 2 for L = O(O)).
Γ = the division hull of ℤP has rank 1 but is not finitely generated; Γ_ℝ is still one-dimensional: finite rank, not finite generation, is the hypothesis.

uses.how: cones of angle (1 − 1/c₄) and the norm growth argument
small points are packed in balls of radius r with r² = max{1, h}/c₃

api.name: NeronTateSpace
api.statement: Γ_ℝ with inner product ⟨·,·⟩_L and the map Γ → Γ_ℝ.

api.name: NeronTateSpace.norm_sq
api.statement: |P|² = ĥ_L(P) for P ∈ Γ.

api.name: NeronTateSpace.finrank

api.name: NeronTateSpace.ker

api.name: NeronTateSpace.mono

api.name: NeronTateSpace.translate
api.statement: For Q ∈ A(ℚ̄), ⟨Γ, Q⟩ has rank ≤ rk Γ + 1, and the space for it contains Γ_ℝ isometrically.

tests.statement: For Γ = A_tors, Γ_ℝ = 0.

tests.name: NeronTateSpace.rank_one
tests.statement: For E: y² = x³ − 2 over ℚ and Γ = E(ℚ) = ℤ·(3, 5), Γ_ℝ ≅ ℝ with |(3,5)|² = ĥ((3,5)) (native Tau Ceti canonical height divided by 2 for L = O(O)).
