nodes.title: Isogeny descends to an algebraically closed base (XY Lemma 3.3)
nodes.statement: Let A₁, A₂ be abelian varieties over an algebraically closed field k and K/k any field extension. If A₁ ⊗_k K is isogenous to A₂ ⊗_k K, then A₁ is isogenous to A₂.
hypotheses: k algebraically closed.
proofSteps: The isogeny is defined over a finitely generated k-algebra R ⊆ K; it extends to a homomorphism of constant abelian schemes over a dense open of Spec R with finite kernel (relative Hom, AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A6).
Specialize at a k-point (k algebraically closed): the specialization is a homomorphism A₁ → A₂ with finite kernel and equal dimensions, hence an isogeny.

sources.match: Spreads an isogeny over a k-variety and specializes at a k-point.

acceptance: For k not algebraically closed the lemma can fail without a rational specialization point; for k algebraically closed every non-empty finite-type k-scheme has a k-point.
Isomorphism is not descended this way in general for non-constant twists, but isogeny classes are.

nodes.title: Isogeny classes defined over two subfields (XY Proposition 3.2)
nodes.statement: Let k be algebraically closed, K/k an extension of finite transcendence degree, and k₁, k₂ algebraically closed intermediate fields with k₁ ∩ k₂ = k. If A₁/k₁ and A₂/k₂ are abelian varieties with A₁ ⊗_{k₁} K isogenous to A₂ ⊗_{k₂} K, then there is an abelian variety A over k, unique up to isogeny, with A₁ isogenous to A ⊗_k k₁ and A₂ isogenous to A ⊗_k k₂.
hypotheses: k algebraically closed; trdeg(K/k) < ∞; k₁, k₂ algebraically closed, k₁ ∩ k₂ = k.
proofSteps: Reduce to K = acl(k₁k₂) by the descent lemma.

Independent case (transcendence defect δ = trdeg k₁ + trdeg k₂ − trdeg k₁k₂ = 0): view A₁ as a family over a k-variety with function field k₁ and A₂ over one with function field k₂; their isogeny over the product forces both families to be isotrivial up to isogeny over k (the printed proof).

For dependent fields, choose finite tuples c,b with k₁=acl(k(c)), k₂=acl(k(b)); let d_i=trdeg(k_i/k), e=trdeg(k₁k₂/k), δ=d₁+d₂−e>0. In an algebraically closed overfield choose a k₁-copy τK independent of K over k₁. The transported isogeny makes A₂ isogenous to τA₂, and k₂∩τk₂=k. Put a=trdeg(c/k(b,τb)). Independence gives trdeg(b,τb,c/k)=2e−d₁, hence the new defect is δ′=2δ−d₁+a. Since a≤d₁−δ, δ′≤δ. Equality would identify the loci of c over k₂ and τk₂ after their compositum extension; subvariety-field-descent then defines that locus over k, contradicting its dimension d₁−δ<d₁. Thus δ′<δ. Apply induction and then the isogeny descent lemma. This is the E18 repair, valid in arbitrary characteristic; it is not the printed independent-fields argument.

sources.match: States that an isogeny class defined over two algebraically closed subfields meeting in k is defined over k, proving it geometrically for algebraically independent subfields.

acceptance: If k₁ = k the statement is the descent lemma.
The hypothesis k₁ ∩ k₂ = k cannot be dropped: for k₁ = k₂ ⊋ k, any non-constant A₁ over k₁ is a counterexample.

nodes.title: Fields of definition of subvarieties (XY Lemma 3.4)
nodes.statement: Let k₁, k₂ be intermediate fields of K/k with k₁ ∩ k₂ = k, Y a variety over k and X ⊆ Y_K a closed subvariety defined over k₁ and over k₂. Then X is defined over k. The linear-algebra core: a K-subspace of V₀ ⊗_k K that descends to k₁ and to k₂ descends to k.
hypotheses: k₁, k₂ intermediate fields of K/k with k₁ ∩ k₂ = k.
proofSteps: Linear core: a finite-dimensional K-subspace W ⊆ V₀ ⊗ K has a unique reduced row echelon basis with respect to a fixed k-basis of V₀; if W descends to k₁ its RREF has entries in k₁, likewise in k₂, so the entries lie in k₁ ∩ k₂ = k.
Apply to the homogeneous ideal of X in each degree after embedding Y in projective space (or on an affine cover), passing to the limit over finite-dimensional pieces.
Mathlib has IsReducedRowEchelon but not its uniqueness; the uniqueness of the reduced row echelon form is part of this node.

sources.match: Proves descent of a subvariety defined over two subfields with intersection k through uniqueness of the reduced row echelon form of a basis of the defining equations in each degree.

acceptance: For k₁ = k₂ = K the hypothesis k₁ ∩ k₂ = k forces K = k.
A line {y = ax} in the plane over K with a ∈ k₁ ∩ k₂ descends; with a ∉ k it is not defined over both.

nodes.title: Minimal fields of definition (XY Corollary 3.5)
nodes.statement: (i) Let K/k be an extension of algebraically closed fields and A an abelian variety over K. There is an algebraically closed intermediate field k_A of finite transcendence degree over k such that, for every algebraically closed intermediate k′, A is defined over k′ up to isogeny iff k_A ⊆ k′. (ii) For a variety Y over k and a closed subvariety X ⊆ Y_K there is an algebraically closed intermediate field k_{X⊆Y_K} of finite transcendence degree over k such that, for every algebraically closed intermediate k′, X is defined over k′ iff k_{X⊆Y_K} ⊆ k′.
hypotheses: K/k algebraically closed fields.
proofSteps: Choose k_A algebraically closed of minimal transcendence degree with A defined over it up to isogeny (A is defined over the algebraic closure of a finitely generated field).

For k′ with A defined over k′, apply the two-subfield proposition to k′ and k_A over k′ ∩ k_A (algebraically closed; source issue E8 corrects the cited reference) to see A is defined over k′ ∩ k_A, so minimality forces k_A ⊆ k′; the dependent-fields repair E18 is needed here.
(ii) is identical with the subvariety descent lemma in place of the two-subfield proposition.

If the ambient algebraically closed K has infinite transcendence degree, choose finite tuples of coefficients defining each variety and isogeny under comparison. The algebraic closure of their compositum has finite transcendence degree, so the preceding intersection theorem applies there before extending back to K.

sources.match: Deduces from the two-subfield statements that the algebraically closed fields of definition (up to isogeny for abelian varieties) have a least element of finite transcendence degree.

acceptance: For A constant, k_A = k.
For the Legendre curve over the algebraic closure of k(t), k_A is the algebraic closure of k(j) = the algebraic closure of k(t).

nodes.title: The field over which X becomes special (XY Proposition 3.6)
nodes.statement: Let K/k be a field extension with k algebraically closed in K, I(K/k) the set of intermediate fields algebraically closed in K, A an abelian variety over K and X ⊆ A_{K̄} a closed subvariety. There is k_{A,X} ∈ I(K/k) such that for every k′ ∈ I(K/k), X is special for A/K/k′ iff k_{A,X} ⊆ k′.
hypotheses: k algebraically closed in K; A/K abelian; X ⊆ A_{K̄} closed.
proofSteps: Over K̄/k̄: if X is special for k′, then X ⊆ tr(A^{K/k′}) + a + C; quotienting by the stabilizer reduces to trivial stabilizer, and then only the implication "special for k′ ⇒ k_A ⊆ k′" holds in the case tr(A^{K/k}) ≠ A; for k′ ⊇ k_A run the second case over k_A through an isogeny A → A₀ ⊗_{k_A} K (repair of the printed first case, source issue E1).
Define k_{A,X} over K̄/k̄ from the minimal fields of A and of the constant part of X (minimal fields, with E18).

In the algebraically closed case let F be the minimal specialness field obtained in the first two steps. For general K, let F″ be the algebraic closure inside K̄ of the compositum of every σF, σ∈Aut(K̄/K), and set k_{A,X}=F″∩K. This is an arbitrary compositum, with no assumed finite orbit. For x∈F″, all roots of its minimal polynomial over K, including inseparable multiplicities, lie in F″; the coefficients therefore lie in F″∩K. Hence F″ is algebraic over that intersection. For relatively algebraically closed k′⊆K its algebraic closure in K̄ is conjugation-stable, and F⊆k̄′ iff F″⊆k̄′ iff k_{A,X}⊆k′. This proves the claimed equivalence (E17 repair).

sources.match: Proves the existence of a least field over which a subvariety becomes special, splitting into the case where the trace is all of A and the case where it is not.

acceptance: If X is a torsion subvariety, k_{A,X} = k.
For A constant and X = C₀ ⊗ K̄ for a curve C₀ over k, k_{A,X} = k; translating C₀ by a non-constant non-torsion point moves k_{A,X} up.

nodes.title: Generic pencil members as polarizations over a subfield (XY Lemma 3.7(1)–(2))
nodes.statement: Let k be algebraically closed, K/k finitely generated with trdeg(K/k) > 1 and (S, M) a polarization with M very ample. There are infinitely many intermediate fields k′ of K/k, algebraically closed in K with trdeg(k′/k) = 1, each with a geometrically integral divisor H ⊆ S_{k′} linearly equivalent to M_{k′} such that H → S_{k′} → S is an isomorphism on generic points; after extending k′ to its algebraic closure k̄′ in K̄ and normalizing ν : H̃ → H_{k̄′}, the pair (H̃, ν^*(M_{k̄′}|_{H_{k̄′}})) is a polarization of Kk̄′/k̄′. Two such fields k₁ ≠ k₂ can be chosen with k₁ ∩ k₂ = k.
hypotheses: k algebraically closed; trdeg(K/k) ≥ 2; M very ample on S.
proofSteps: For s₀, s₁ ∈ Γ(S, M) with s₁/s₀ non-constant, the blow-up of the base locus fibres S over ℙ¹; k′ = k(s₁/s₀) after algebraic closure in K, and H is the generic member, geometrically integral by Bertini.

Two distinct fields: fix s₀ with geometrically integral divisor and choose s₁, s₂ with s₁/s₀, s₂/s₀ algebraically independent (a general projection of S to ℙ² is dominant); the pencils give k₁ ≠ k₂ with k₁ ∩ k₂ = k (source issue E5 of the XY extraction: the printed proof builds only one).
Normalize the geometric generic member and pull M back; ampleness is preserved by finite pullback (source issue E19).

sources.match: Builds from a pencil ⟨s₀, s₁⟩ of sections of M the field k′ = k(s₁/s₀) (algebraically closed in K) and the generic member H of the pencil as a polarization of the function field over k′.

acceptance: For trdeg(K/k) = 2 and S = ℙ², the pencils of lines through a point give k′ = k(y/x) and H the generic line.
Without normalization the member H_{k̄′} may be non-normal and is not a polarization in the sense of §1.1 (E19).

nodes.title: Heights decrease on generic pencil members (XY Lemma 3.7, height inequality)
nodes.statement: For (k′, H) as in the pencil lemma, every abelian variety A over K with symmetric ample L and every subvariety X ⊆ A_{K̄}: ĥ^M_L(X) ≥ ĥ^{M_{k′}|_H}_L(X), the left side computed for K/k with (S, M) and the right side for Kk̄′/k̄′ with the normalized pencil member.
hypotheses: (k′, H) from the pencil lemma; A/K abelian; X ⊆ A_{K̄}.
proofSteps: Write ĥ^M_L(X) as a limit of ℒ^{dim X+1} · (π^*M)^{dim S−1} · 𝒳 over models (parent RP.0).
Base change to k′ and replace one factor π^*M by π^{-1}(H): the intersection with 𝒳_{k′} contains 𝒳*_H plus an effective cycle; nefness of ℒ and π^*M makes the dropped term ≥ 0 (SF.5 positivity).
Identify the remaining term with the height for the normalized pencil member, defined by the same intersection formula even before normalization (E19).

sources.locator: Lemma 3.7, height inequality, p. 17; proof p. 18 (arXiv v1)
sources.match: Compares the canonical height of a subvariety for the original polarization with that for the generic pencil member by replacing one factor π^*M by the divisor of the pencil and dropping an effective cycle.

acceptance: Equality holds when X is defined over k′ and the pencil is in general position (no excess part).
Only the inequality is used: small points for K/k remain small for Kk̄′/k̄′.

nodes.title: Lowering the transcendence degree (XY Proposition 3.1)
nodes.statement: Let k be algebraically closed, K/k finitely generated with trdeg(K/k) ≥ 2 and A an abelian variety over K. There are intermediate fields k₁, k₂ of K/k, algebraically closed in K with trdeg(k_i/k) = 1, such that for every closed subvariety X ⊆ A_{K̄}, the geometric Bogomolov statement holds for (A/K/k, X) if it holds for (A_{Kk̄₁}/Kk̄₁/k̄₁, X) and (A_{Kk̄₂}/Kk̄₂/k̄₂, X).
hypotheses: k algebraically closed; trdeg(K/k) ≥ 2.
proofSteps: Take k₁ ≠ k₂ from two pencils with k₁ ∩ k₂ = k (E5).
If X has dense small points for A/K/k, then by the pencil height inequality it has dense small points over Kk̄_i/k̄_i; by hypothesis X is special for A/K/k_i, i = 1, 2.
By the special-field proposition k_{A,X} ⊆ k₁ ∩ k₂ = k, so X is special for A/K/k (source issue E10 fixes a missing negation in the printed contradiction).
Alternatively the shorter independent transcendence-degree-one argument recorded in the XY extraction can replace the field-theoretic step.

sources.match: Chooses two pencils whose fields meet in k; small points over K/k stay small over each Kk̄_i/k̄_i by the height inequality, so X is special over both k_i, hence over k by the minimality of the field over which X becomes special.

acceptance: Induction on the transcendence degree reduces the geometric Bogomolov conjecture to trdeg(K/k) = 1.
The two fields must meet in k; one pencil is not enough.

nodes.title: Multi-sections and torsion multi-sections
nodes.statement: Let π : 𝒜 → S be an abelian scheme over a smooth projective curve S over a field k (more generally a smooth curve). A multi-section of π is a closed integral subscheme 𝒯 ⊆ 𝒜 finite and flat over S. It is torsion of order m if the tautological point of 𝒜_𝒯(𝒯) it defines is torsion of exact order m. A torsion multi-section is the Zariski closure of a torsion point of the generic fibre A(K̄), and one of order m lies in 𝒜[m].
hypotheses: π : 𝒜 → S abelian scheme over a smooth projective curve S over a field.
proofSteps: The closure of a torsion point of order m lies in the closed subgroup scheme 𝒜[m], which is finite over S; an integral closed subscheme finite and dominant over a smooth curve is flat. Over higher-dimensional normal bases flatness can fail, which is why the definition is made over curves.

sources.match: Defines multi-sections of an abelian scheme and torsion multi-sections, and notes that torsion multi-sections are closures of torsion points in the kernel of multiplication.

acceptance: The zero section is a torsion multi-section of order 1 and degree 1.
For the Legendre family in characteristic different from 2 over ℙ¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}, the closure of the 2-torsion point (0, 0) is a torsion multi-section of order 2 and degree 1.
The closure of a non-torsion section is a multi-section that is not torsion.

uses.how: the numerical class of a torsion multi-section is a multiple of the top power of the rigidified symmetric bundle
fibres of the summation map over torsion points are controlled through torsion multi-sections of 𝒜′

tests.statement: The closure of a non-torsion section is a multi-section that is not torsion.

nodes.title: Numerical class of a torsion multi-section (XY Proposition 4.2)
nodes.statement: Let S be a smooth projective curve over a field k, π : 𝒜 → S an abelian scheme of relative dimension g ≥ 1, ℒ a symmetric rigidified line bundle on 𝒜 and 𝒯 a torsion multi-section. Then [ℒ]^g ≡ (deg(ℒ_η)/deg(𝒯/S))·[𝒯] numerically as 1-cycles on 𝒜, where deg(ℒ_η) is the degree of ℒ on the generic fibre.
hypotheses: S smooth projective curve over k; π abelian scheme of relative dimension g ≥ 1; ℒ symmetric rigidified.
proofSteps: Numerical classes of line bundles on 𝒜 are generated by rigidified ones and pullbacks π^*N (rigidification along the zero section).

For rigidified ℳ, split 2ℳ into symmetric and antisymmetric parts so that [m]^*ℳ ≅ m^iℳ, i = 2 or 1 (source issue E11); [m]^*[ℒ]^g pushes forward with factor m^{2g} while ℳ · [ℒ]^g scales by m^{2g+i}, forcing ℳ · [ℒ]^g = 0; likewise ℳ · [𝒯] = 0 since a torsion multi-section restricts ℳ to a torsion bundle (A1).
For ℳ = π^*N compare degrees: π^*N · [ℒ]^g = deg N · deg ℒ_η and π^*N · [𝒯] = deg N · deg(𝒯/S).

sources.match: Proves that a torsion multi-section is numerically proportional to the top power of a symmetric rigidified bundle by testing against rigidified bundles (both sides vanish, by the projection formula for multiplication) and against pullbacks from the base (degrees agree).

acceptance: For an elliptic scheme over a smooth projective curve, take the rigidified normalization of O(2·0), twisting by a base bundle if necessary. Its numerical class is 2[0], consistent with generic degree 2 and degree-one zero section.
Any two torsion multi-sections of degree 1 are numerically equivalent.
Grushevsky–Zakharov prove the rational-equivalence version over higher-dimensional bases; only the numerical version over a curve is needed.

nodes.title: Yamaki’s reduction to the nowhere degenerate trace-free part
nodes.statement: Let k be algebraically closed, B normal projective of positive dimension, K=k(B), and A an abelian variety over K̄. Let 𝔪⊆A be its maximal nowhere-degenerate abelian subvariety, meaning potential good reduction at every geometric divisorial valuation in Yamaki’s setting, and let t be the image of the geometric K̄/k-trace. Then geometric Bogomolov holds for A iff it holds for 𝔪 iff it holds for 𝔪/t. These are geometric objects; they may require a finite extension of a chosen field of definition. In transcendence degree one the nowhere-degenerate quotient acquires an abelian-scheme model after a finite extension.
hypotheses: k algebraically closed; K = k(B) for a normal projective B of dimension ≥ 1.
proofSteps: The statement was checked against Yamaki’s arXiv v5; its proof uses Gubler’s tropical equidistribution at places of bad reduction (for the step from A to 𝔪) and Yamaki’s analysis of closed subvarieties of abelian schemes over constant varieties, starting from the equivalence of dense small points and canonical height 0 (the Zhang–Gubler inequalities).
No roadmap of the atlas plans Gubler’s tropical equidistribution; the theorem is an input here, recorded as a gap.

sources.locator: §5, condition (d), p. 22 (arXiv v1), citing Yamaki, J. reine angew. Math. 2018, Theorem 1.5
sources.match: Uses Yamaki’s theorem to reduce the geometric Bogomolov conjecture to abelian varieties with good reduction everywhere and trivial trace.

Proves that the geometric Bogomolov conjecture for an abelian variety over the function field of a normal projective variety is equivalent to that for its maximal nowhere degenerate abelian subvariety and to that for the quotient of the latter by the image of the trace.

acceptance: If A has good reduction everywhere and trivial trace, 𝔪 = A and t = 0, and the statement is trivial.
For A totally degenerate at some place, A has trivial trace and the conclusion for A is Gubler’s theorem.

nodes.title: Reduction of the geometric Bogomolov conjecture to conditions (a)–(d)
nodes.statement: To prove that every closed X ⊆ A_{K̄} with dense small points is special, it suffices to treat the case where (a) trdeg(K/k) = 1, (b) the model S is a smooth projective curve, (c) A has semistable reduction over S, (d) A has trivial geometric K̄/k-trace and good reduction over S; and X may moreover be assumed defined over K after a finite extension of K.
hypotheses: k algebraically closed; K/k finitely generated with trdeg ≥ 1.
proofSteps: (a) by induction with the transcendence reduction; (b) the regular projective model of a function field of one variable is unique.
(c) semistable reduction holds after a finite extension of K (NeronModels R11.3), which preserves small points and speciality (parent RP.0 base change).
(d) Yamaki’s reduction passes to 𝔪/t, which has good reduction and trivial trace; X is defined over a finite extension of K.

sources.match: Reduces the theorem to transcendence degree one, a smooth projective curve model, semistable reduction, trivial trace and good reduction, by Proposition 3.1, the semistable reduction theorem and Yamaki’s theorem.

acceptance: Every step preserves both the hypothesis (dense small points) and the conclusion (special).
After (d), special means torsion subvariety.

nodes.title: Iterated sums X_m of a subvariety
nodes.statement: For a nonempty closed subvariety X of an abelian variety A and m ≥ 1, X_m is the image of the addition morphism f_m : X^m → A, (x₁, …, x_m) ↦ x₁ + ⋯ + x_m, and X₀ = {0}. Then dim X_{m−1} ≤ dim X_m ≤ dim X_{m−1} + dim X.
hypotheses: X ⊆ A nonempty and closed.
proofSteps: The addition map is proper, so X_m is closed; X_m = X_{m−1} + X gives the dimension bounds.

sources.match: Defines the iterated sums of X as images of addition maps and records the dimension inequalities.

acceptance: X₀ = {0} and X₁ = X.
For an Abel–Jacobi curve C ⊆ J of genus g through 0, C_m is the image of the m-th symmetric power, of dimension min(m, g), and C_g = J.
For X={x} with x non-torsion, X_m={mx} has dimension zero and need not be a subgroup. The hypothesis 0∈X in the stabilization API is essential; X={0} itself stabilizes immediately.

uses.how: the sums stabilize at a torsion subvariety when X has dense small points
the summation X_{r−1} × X → A′ is studied fibre by fibre

api.name: IteratedSum
api.statement: X_m ⊆ A closed for m ≥ 0.

api.name: IteratedSum.dim_mono
api.statement: dim X_{m−1} ≤ dim X_m ≤ dim X_{m−1} + dim X.

api.name: IteratedSum.stabilize
api.statement: For 0 ∈ X irreducible, the X_m increase and stabilize at the abelian subvariety generated by X, within dim A steps.

api.name: IteratedSum.translate
api.statement: (X − x₀)_m = X_m − m x₀.

tests.name: IteratedSum.zero
tests.statement: X₀ = {0} and X₁ = X.

tests.name: IteratedSum.curve_jacobian
tests.statement: For an Abel–Jacobi curve C ⊆ J of genus g through 0, C_m is the image of the m-th symmetric power, of dimension min(m, g), and C_g = J.

tests.name: IteratedSum.point
tests.statement: For X={x} with x non-torsion, X_m={mx} has dimension zero and need not be a subgroup. The hypothesis 0∈X in the stabilization API is essential; X={0} itself stabilizes immediately.

nodes.title: The sums become a torsion subvariety (XY Lemma 5.3)
nodes.statement: Assume (a)–(d), dim X ≥ 1, X irreducible and X with dense small points. There is a unique integer r ≥ 1 with dim X_{r−1} < dim X_r and X_r a torsion subvariety of A. After a torsion translation and a finite extension of K one may assume (e): A′ := X_r is an abelian subvariety of A and dim X_{r−1} < dim X_r.
hypotheses: (a)–(d); X irreducible with dim X ≥ 1 (source issue E4: the printed lemma omits it) and dense small points.
proofSteps: Choose any x₀∈X; the sums X_m−mx₀ increase and eventually stabilize at the abelian subvariety B generated by X−x₀. Let r be the first stabilization index. No assertion that one chosen point has height zero is needed.

Products of dense arbitrarily small sets map to dense arbitrarily small sets in X_r. Since X_r is a translate B+t, its image in A/B has height zero. Trivial geometric trace makes that image torsion; choose a torsion lift, so X_r is a torsion translate of B.
Its height is 0, and trivial trace makes height-0 points torsion (parent RP.1 kernel), so t is torsion mod B and X_r is a torsion subvariety; uniqueness of r because dim X ≥ 1 forces the first jump.

sources.locator: Lemma 5.3, pp. 23–24, and condition (e), pp. 24–25 (arXiv v1)
sources.match: Shows that the iterated sums of a subvariety with dense small points stabilize at a torsion translate of an abelian subvariety, using heights on a product B × C and trivial trace.

acceptance: For X a point the conclusion fails: X_m = {mx} never jumps (E4).

For a positive-dimensional abelian subvariety X through zero, r=1. For a genus-two ample curve C through zero in its abelian surface Jacobian, C+C=J and r=2. A smooth elliptic curve through zero in an abelian variety is a subgroup, so the former non-subgroup elliptic example cannot occur.

nodes.title: Relative dimension of the summation map and its jump locus
nodes.statement: Under (e), the summation morphism f : X_{r−1} × X → A′ has relative dimension e = dim X_{r−1} + dim X − dim A′ < dim X, and A′_{e+1} = {y ∈ A′ : dim f^{-1}(y) ≥ e + 1} is closed of codimension ≥ 2 in A′.
proofSteps: f is surjective onto A′ = X_r, so its generic fibre dimension is e = dim X_{r−1} + dim X − dim A′, which is < dim X since dim X_{r−1} < dim A′.
Upper semicontinuity of fibre dimension makes A′_{e+1} closed; the dimension count dim f^{-1}(A′_{e+1}) ≤ dim(X_{r−1} × X) gives codimension ≥ 2 when combined with irreducibility of X_{r−1} × X.

sources.match: Computes the generic relative dimension of the summation map onto A′ and shows that the locus of larger fibres is closed of codimension at least two.

acceptance: If X = A′ is already an abelian subvariety (r = 1), X_{0} × X = X and e = 0.
Torsion points off A′_{e+1} are dense in A′ (codimension ≥ 2 complement; prime-to-p torsion is dense).

nodes.title: Torsion fibres have height zero (XY Proposition 5.4)
nodes.statement: Under (a)–(e), for every torsion point t ∈ A′(K̄) ∖ A′_{e+1}(K̄) of order prime to char k (the printed proposition allows every torsion t, but its proof treats only prime-to-p orders; source issue E2 of the XY extraction), every irreducible component of the fibre f^{-1}(t) ⊆ (X_{r−1} × X)_{K̄} has canonical height 0 in (A × A)_{K̄}.
hypotheses: (a)–(e); t torsion of order prime to char k, off the jump locus.
proofSteps: Work on Néron models: 𝒜′_N for A′ and ℬ_N = 𝒜 ×_S 𝒜′_N for B ⊆ A × A, with the generic isomorphism A × A′ → B, (x, t) ↦ (x, t − x); the summation h is the flat second projection and 𝒴 the closure there, never a possibly nonsmooth embedded closure (source issue E16).

Xie–Yuan’s non-proper intersection inequality (their Proposition 2.1, owned by SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.5) bounds Σ m_i[𝒵_i] · [ℒ_ℬ]^{e+1} ≤ h^*[𝒯] · [𝒴] · [ℒ_ℬ]^{e+1} for the torsion multi-section 𝒯 of t (E13).

Replace [𝒯] by a[ℒ_{𝒜′}]^{dim A′} (numerical class of torsion multi-sections); ĥ(Y) = 0 for Y = X_{r−1} × X (dense small points and Zhang–Gubler) forces [𝒵_i] · [ℒ_ℬ]^{e+1} = 0, hence ĥ(Z_i) = 0 (E14).
Only t of order prime to the characteristic is treated: the multi-section must be étale (source issue E2).

sources.match: Bounds the components of the fibre over a torsion multi-section by an intersection inequality for non-proper intersections, replaces the multi-section by a multiple of the top power of the rigidified bundle, and concludes that the components have zero height.

acceptance: For t = 0 the fibre f^{-1}(0) contains the antidiagonal-type locus {(y, −x)}; its components have height 0 when X has dense small points.
In characteristic p, p-power torsion is excluded; prime-to-p torsion off A′_{e+1} is still dense, which is all §5.3 uses.

nodes.title: The geometric Bogomolov conjecture under (a)–(d), by induction on dim X
nodes.statement: Assume (a)–(d). Every closed irreducible X ⊆ A_{K̄} with a dense set of small points is a torsion subvariety.
hypotheses: (a)–(d); X irreducible closed with dense small points.
proofSteps: dim X = 0: dense small points mean ĥ(x) = 0, and over a function field the kernel of the Néron–Tate height is torsion plus trace points (parent RP.1), so with trivial trace x is torsion.

dim X ≥ 1: arrange (e). For prime-to-p torsion t ∈ A′ off A′_{e+1}, the components of f^{-1}(t) have height 0, hence dense small points (Zhang–Gubler converse, source issue E3), and dimension e < dim X; by induction (applied in A × A, which again satisfies (a)–(d)) they are torsion subvarieties.

These t are dense in A′, so X_{r−1} × X contains a dense set of torsion points; Manin–Mumford for abelian varieties with trivial trace in every characteristic (parent RP.5: Hrushovski, Pink–Rössler; Scanlon’s all-torsion form) makes X_{r−1} × X, hence X, a torsion subvariety. Torsion inside the translated components may have p-primary part.

sources.match: Proves the good-reduction trace-free case by induction on the dimension: fibres of the summation over prime-to-p torsion points are torsion by induction, so X_{r−1} × X has dense torsion and Manin–Mumford concludes.

acceptance: For X a torsion coset the hypothesis holds and the conclusion is immediate.
The induction runs on A × A, not on A: the hypotheses (a)–(d) are stable under products.

nodes.title: The geometric Bogomolov conjecture (Xie–Yuan Theorem 1.1)
nodes.statement: Let k be algebraically closed, K/k finitely generated of transcendence degree ≥ 1, A an abelian variety over K and X a nonempty closed irreducible subvariety of A_{K̄}. If X contains a dense set of small points of A/K/k, then X is special.
hypotheses: k algebraically closed; K/k finitely generated of transcendence degree ≥ 1; X ⊆ A_{K̄} closed.
proofSteps: Reduce to (a)–(d) and to X irreducible and defined over K.
Apply the good-reduction case: X is a torsion subvariety of the trace-free quotient; lifting through Yamaki’s reduction makes X special for A/K/k.
The converse (special ⇒ dense small points) is the easy direction.

sources.match: Proves the geometric Bogomolov conjecture in all characteristics and finite transcendence degree, without Betti maps: reduction to transcendence degree one, Yamaki’s reduction to good reduction and trivial trace, and an induction on dimension ending in Manin–Mumford.

acceptance: A special subvariety tr(Y ⊗ K̄) + T has dense small points, so the theorem is an equivalence.
In characteristic 0 over a curve it agrees with Gao–Habegger’s Theorem 1.1.
For constant A = A₀ ⊗ K every subvariety of the form Y ⊗ K̄ is special, so the trace term cannot be omitted from the conclusion.

nodes.title: Small-points bound for potentially big families (Yuan Theorem 4.2)
nodes.statement: (1) Let S be a quasi-projective variety over a number field K, π : X → S a smooth relative curve, L̄ a nef adelic line bundle on X/ℤ and M̄ an adelic line bundle on S/ℤ. If L̄ is potentially big over S, there are a non-empty open U ⊆ S and c₁, c₂ > 0 such that for every y ∈ U(K̄), #{x ∈ X(K̄) : π(x) = y, h_{L̄}(x) ≤ c₁h_{M̄}(y)} ≤ c₂. (2) Let S be a positive-dimensional quasi-projective variety over a field k, π : X → S a smooth relative curve, L̄ nef adelic on X/k potentially big over S and M̄ adelic on S/k. There are a non-empty open U ⊆ S and c₁, c₂ > 0 such that for every point y ∈ U of dimension one (with function field k(y) of transcendence degree 1 over k), #{x ∈ X_y(k(y)‾) : h_{L̄|X_y}(x) ≤ c₁·deĝ(M̄|_y)} ≤ c₂, heights normalized over k(y)/k.
hypotheses: π : X → S smooth relative curve; L̄ nef and potentially big over S.
proofSteps: Potential bigness gives m with m⊠L̄ big on X^m_{/S} (ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeightsPartII AH.12).

The Yuan–Zhang height inequality (AH.4, part (1)) gives ε > 0 and an effective divisor Z of a multiple of m⊠L̄ − επ^*M̄ such that points of X^m_{/S} off Z satisfy h_{m⊠L̄} ≥ εh_{M̄}∘π; for a strict inequality defining a closed exceptional set, add to M̄ an ample model bundle of positive degree on every point (source issues E20–E21 of the Yuan extraction).

Over a dense open U of S the fibres Z_y are proper in X_y^m with bounded degree; a set Σ of small points with Σ^m ⊆ Z_y has |Σ| ≤ (deg Z_y)^{1/d} by the product-grid bound, applied to each finite subset of Σ so that Σ itself is finite (source issue E22: the printed proof assumes the finiteness the lemma concludes).

sources.locator: Theorem 4.2(1)–(2), p. 64; proof pp. 65–67 (author manuscript 21 August 2024)
sources.match: Bounds uniformly over a dense open of the base the number of points of small height in the fibres of a family of curves carrying a potentially big nef adelic line bundle, by the height inequality on a fibre power and the product-grid bound.

acceptance: The constants depend on the family and the bundles, not on y ∈ U.

Potential bigness is necessary: for a constant family X = C × S over a positive-dimensional base with L̄ pulled back from C, the number of x with h_{L̄}(x) ≤ c₁h_{M̄}(y) tends to infinity with h_{M̄}(y), so no uniform c₂ exists; such an L̄ is not potentially big.

nodes.title: Non-isotrivial function-field points
nodes.statement: Let U be a scheme over ℤ, K a function field of one variable over a field k and k′ the algebraic closure of k in K. A morphism y : Spec K → U is non-isotrivial if it does not factor through Spec K → Spec k′. When U is a finite-type k-scheme and y is a k-morphism, this says that the closure of the image of y is a curve (a point of dimension one).
hypotheses: K/k of transcendence degree 1.
proofSteps: Use the factoring predicate as stated. Finite extension of K preserves it. For finite-type k-schemes, the image has dimension at most one; quasi-finite k-morphisms preserve this dimension, giving the composition API.

sources.locator: Explanation of Theorem 4.10, p. 82 (author manuscript 21 August 2024)
sources.match: Defines non-isotrivial morphisms from the spectrum of a function field to a base scheme as those not factoring through the algebraic closure of the constant field.

acceptance: For U = 𝔸¹_k and K = k(t), the point t is non-isotrivial and every constant c ∈ k is isotrivial.

For k = ℝ and K = ℂ(t) (constant field k′ = ℂ), the point i ∈ 𝔸¹(K) is not in k but factors through Spec k′, so it is isotrivial: the criterion is factoring through the algebraic closure of k in K, not through k.
If U = Spec k, no point is non-isotrivial.

uses.how: the integral small-points bound holds for all non-isotrivial points of a dense open
a curve with level structure is non-isotrivial iff its moduli point is non-isotrivial

api.name: IsNonIsotrivialPoint
api.statement: The predicate on y : Spec K → U.

api.name: IsNonIsotrivialPoint.comp
api.statement: For a quasi-finite morphism U→V of finite-type k-schemes and a K-point y of U, y is non-isotrivial iff its image in V is non-isotrivial. All morphisms here are k-morphisms.

api.statement: Preserved under finite extension K′/K.

api.name: IsNonIsotrivialPoint.closed_point
api.statement: For U of finite type over k, y is isotrivial iff its image is a closed point.

tests.statement: For U = 𝔸¹_k and K = k(t), the point t is non-isotrivial and every constant c ∈ k is isotrivial.

tests.name: IsNonIsotrivialPoint.algebraic_constant

tests.name: IsNonIsotrivialPoint.point_base
tests.statement: If U = Spec k, no point is non-isotrivial.

nodes.title: Integral small-points bound across characteristics (Yuan Theorem 4.10)
nodes.statement: Let S be a quasi-projective flat integral scheme over ℤ, π : X → S a smooth relative curve, L̄ a nef adelic line bundle on X/ℤ and M̄ adelic on S/ℤ. If L̄ is potentially big on X/S, there are a non-empty open U ⊆ S and c₁, c₂ > 0 such that for every function field K of one variable over any field k and every non-isotrivial y : Spec K → U, #{x ∈ X_y(K̄) : h_{L̄|X_y}(x) ≤ c₁·deĝ(M̄|_y)} ≤ c₂, where the restrictions pass through S_ℚ/ℚ or S_{𝔽_p}/𝔽_p and then S_k/k, and heights are normalized over K/k.
hypotheses: S quasi-projective flat integral over ℤ; L̄ nef, potentially big over S.
proofSteps: Choose m with m⊠L̄ big on X^m_{/S} over ℤ and ε > 0 with m⊠L̄ − επ^*M̄ big; a multiple has a non-zero effective section s over ℤ, Z = div(s).
Restriction across characteristics (AH.12) preserves effectivity: for every non-isotrivial y, small points of (X^m)_y lie in Z_y, with strict inequality as in E21.
The fibres Z_y over a dense open U are proper with degree bounded by the degree over ℤ; the product-grid bound concludes as in Theorem 4.2.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.10 and proof, pp. 81–83 (author manuscript 21 August 2024)
sources.match: States the small-points bound uniformly for all function fields of one variable and all non-isotrivial points of a dense open of an integral base, proving it like Theorem 4.2(2) from an effective section of a multiple of m⊠L̄ − εM̄ defined over ℤ.

acceptance: The constants are independent of k and of the characteristic.
Isotrivial points must be excluded: for y factoring through k′, heights of constant points are 0 and deĝ(M̄|_y) = 0.

nodes.title: Potential bigness implies non-degeneracy of fibre powers (Yuan Proposition 4.16)
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, S a quasi-projective normal k-variety, ψ : A → S an abelian scheme of relative dimension r, ι : Y → A a generically finite morphism from a quasi-projective k-variety, L a symmetric ψ-ample line bundle rigidified along zero and L̄ its invariant adelic extension over k. If Y → S is projective flat with geometrically integral generic fibre of dimension e, L|_Y has positive top degree on the generic fibre, and the relative Deligne pairing ⟨(ι^*L̄)^{e+1}⟩ is big on S/k, then ι^m : Y^m_{/S} → A^m_{/S} is non-degenerate for every m ≥ dim S.
hypotheses: as stated; non-degeneracy in the adelic sense (bigness of ι^*L̄ on Y/k).
The fibre-power exponent m is a positive integer, including when dim S=0.
proofSteps: By the potential-bigness criterion, m⊠ι^*L̄ is big on Y^m_{/S} for every m ≥ dim S.
Non-degeneracy of ι^m means bigness of (ι^m)^*(m⊠L̄) = m⊠ι^*L̄, i.e. exactly this (AH.5 non-degeneracy).

sources.match: Deduces non-degeneracy of fibre powers from bigness of the Deligne pairing through the criterion for potential bigness; the structure morphism Y → S is written π where ψ∘ι is meant (source issue E26 of the Yuan extraction).

acceptance: For S=Spec k, invariant adelic non-degeneracy is geometric bigness: a closed positive-dimensional subvariety with an ample restricted bundle satisfies it, including an abelian subvariety itself. No abelian-subvariety-free condition is required.
Over ℂ the conclusion is full Betti rank of Y^m_{/S}, matching Gao’s criterion for fibred powers.

nodes.title: Non-degeneracy of Abel, difference and Faltings–Zhang powers (Yuan Theorem 4.17)
nodes.statement: Let k be any field, S a quasi-projective integral k-variety, π : X → S a smooth relative curve of genus g > 1 with maximal variation, J = Pic⁰_{X/S}, and α a line bundle of positive relative degree defining i_α : X → J. Then the following are non-degenerate: (1) i_α^m : X^m_{/S} → J^m_{/S} for m ≥ dim S; (2) i_Δ^m : (X_X)^m_{/X} → (J_X)^m_{/X} for m ≥ dim S + 1, with i_Δ(x, y) = (x, y − x); (3) i_{ω−Q}^m : (X_J)^m_{/J} → (J_J)^m_{/J} for m ≥ dim S + g, with the universal shift τ; (4) the Faltings–Zhang map X^{m+1}_{/S} → J^m_{/S} for m ≥ dim S + 1; (5) τ_m : X^m_{/S} ×_S J → J^m_{/S} for m ≥ dim S + g. S may be non-normal (restrict to a normal dense open). Here τ_m(x₁,…,x_m,y)=((2g−2)x₁−ω+y,x₂−x₁,…,x_m−x₁), with all divisor classes taken in the relative Jacobian, and m≥1 throughout.
hypotheses: g > 1; π smooth with maximal variation; α of positive relative degree.
The fibre-power exponent m is a positive integer, including when dim S=0.
proofSteps: Potential bigness of i_α^*Θ̄, i_Δ^*Θ̄_X and τ^*Θ̄_J (AH.12 theta potential bigness), with the Deligne pairings computed by the theta identities (AH.9).
Apply the fibre-power proposition to each map; the thresholds on m are dim of the respective base (S, X or J), i.e. dim S, dim S + 1 and dim S + g.
The Faltings–Zhang and shifted Faltings–Zhang maps are the difference and shift maps composed with fibre products (JacobianChallengePartII JC2, JC5).

sources.match: Proves non-degeneracy of five maps built from a curve family with maximal variation, from potential bigness of the theta pullbacks and Proposition 4.16, in every characteristic.

acceptance: In characteristic 0 over ℂ, part (4) recovers Gao’s non-degeneracy of D_M(C_S^{[M+1]}) (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuliPartII B4) with a different threshold.
Maximal variation cannot be dropped: for an isotrivial family the moduli map is constant and the Deligne pairing is not big.

nodes.title: The relative Bogomolov small-points property
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field (base k = ℤ) or a function field of one variable over k, S a normal quasi-projective K-variety, A → S an abelian scheme, ι : Y → A generically finite and L a symmetric relatively ample line bundle rigidified along zero, with fibrewise Néron–Tate height ĥ_L. For ε > 0 put Y(L, ε) = {y ∈ Y(K̄) : ĥ_L(ι(y)) ≤ ε}. ι has the small-points property if Y(L, ε) is not Zariski dense in Y for some ε > 0. The property does not depend on L: for two such L, L′ there is n > 0 with n^{-1}ĥ_L ≤ ĥ_{L′} ≤ nĥ_L on A(K̄).
hypotheses: as stated.
proofSteps: Fibrewise Néron–Tate heights of L are the heights of its invariant adelic extension (AH.5).
Two symmetric relatively ample rigidified bundles dominate positive multiples of each other on the generic fibre, and canonical heights are monotone and linear in the bundle.

nodes.title: Arithmetic potential bigness gives the small-points property (Yuan Proposition 4.18)
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field or a function field of one variable over k, S a normal quasi-projective K-variety, A → S an abelian scheme, ι : Y → A generically finite and L symmetric relatively ample rigidified with canonical adelic extension L̄ over k (ℤ in the arithmetic case). If Y → S is projective flat with geometrically integral generic fibre of dimension e, L|_Y is big on that fibre, and the relative Deligne pairing ⟨(ι^*L̄)^{e+1}⟩_{Y/S} is big on S/k, then ι^m : Y^m_{/S} → A^m_{/S} has the small-points property for every m ≥ dim_K S + 1. Bigness over k is an explicit hypothesis; relative variation over K alone does not replace it.
hypotheses: as stated, with bigness on S/k.
proofSteps: By the criterion, m⊠ι^*L̄ is big on Y^m_{/S} over k for m ≥ dim_K S + 1 (one more than the geometric threshold, since the base now has absolute dimension dim_K S + 1).

The height inequality (AH.4 part (1)) applied to m⊠ι^*L̄ and an auxiliary adelic Ā of height ≥ 1 at every point gives ε > 0 and a dense open U ⊆ Y^m_{/S} with h_{m⊠L̄} ≥ ε on U(K̄); points of Y^m all of whose coordinates have height ≤ ε/(2m) lie in the proper closed complement, so small points are not dense.

sources.match: Shows that bigness of the arithmetic Deligne pairing over the base gives the relative small-points property for high fibre powers, via the height inequality.

acceptance: In the function-field case the hypothesis is bigness over the constant field k; a constant family fails it.
The structure morphism is ψ∘ι, misprinted as π (E26).

nodes.title: Relative Bogomolov for curve families (Yuan Theorem 4.19)
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, or a function field of one variable over k with k its field of constants, S a quasi-projective K-variety and π : X → S a smooth relative curve of genus g > 1 with maximal variation — in the function-field case, maximal variation over k (the moduli morphism generically finite on a projective model of S over k). Let α have positive relative degree. Then the small-points property holds for: (1) i_α^m for m ≥ dim S + 1; (2) i_Δ^m for m ≥ dim S + 2; (3) i_{ω−Q}^m for m ≥ dim S + g + 1; (4) the Faltings–Zhang map X^{m+1}_{/S} → J^m_{/S} for m ≥ dim S + 2; (5) τ_m for m ≥ dim S + g + 1.
hypotheses: g > 1; maximal variation (over k in the function-field case); α of positive relative degree.
proofSteps: Theta potential bigness over k (AH.12) gives bigness of the Deligne pairings over k; the thresholds rise by one from those of Theorem 4.17 because the base is now absolute.
Apply the arithmetic potential-bigness proposition.

Function fields: the counterexample recorded as E1 (a constant family over K with K-relative but not k-relative variation) shows the printed K-relative hypothesis is false; the plan states the corrected hypothesis.

sources.match: Establishes the relative Bogomolov small-points property for the five maps attached to a curve family with maximal variation; in the function-field case the printed hypothesis of maximal variation over K is too weak and must be read over the constant field (source issue E1 of the Yuan extraction).

acceptance: For S a point over a number field, part (1) applies to the Abel image of C with m=1. Part (4) first applies at m=2, to the difference image of C³ in J². For genus two C−C=J, so claiming non-dense small points on that m=1 image would be false.
The function-field branches hold only with maximal variation over the constants (E1).

nodes.title: The twice-theta Néron–Tate normalization of a curve
nodes.statement: Let C be a smooth projective curve of genus g > 1 over a number field or a function field of one variable K, J its Jacobian and x₀ ∈ C(K̄). θ_{x₀} is the image of C^{g−1} → J, (x_i) ↦ Σ x_i − (g − 1)x₀, and Θ = O(θ_{x₀} + [−1]^*θ_{x₀}) is symmetric ample, independent of x₀ and descends to J (it is the canonical twice-theta bundle). The Néron–Tate height of the curve is ĥ = ½ĥ_Θ, with ĥ_Θ the Tate limit of a Weil height of Θ in the normalization of heights over K (absolute over ℚ for number fields, over K/k for function fields).
hypotheses: g > 1; K a global field (number field or function field of one variable).
proofSteps: The twice-theta bundle is the canonical one of JacobianChallengePartII JC3 (independent of x₀ by the theorem of the square).
Tate’s limit of the Weil height of Θ (parent RP.0); halve it.

sources.match: Defines the theta divisor by a base point, the symmetric twice-theta bundle, its independence of the base point and the Néron–Tate height as half the canonical height of that bundle, with the normalization of Weil heights.

acceptance: For a genus-two curve and x₀ a Weierstrass point, θ_{x₀} is symmetric and Θ = O(2θ_{x₀}).
Using ĥ_Θ instead of ½ĥ_Θ doubles every height; the uniform constants c₁ are stated for the halved height.

uses.how: the uniform bound is stated for ĥ(x − α)

nodes.title: Projective heights over function fields with fixed constants
nodes.statement: Let K/k be a function field of transcendence degree one and x = [x₀ : ⋯ : x_n] with coordinates in a finite extension K′/K. Put h(x) = [K′ : K]^{-1} Σ_v log max_i ‖x_i‖_v, where v runs over the closed points of the regular projective k-curve with function field K′ and ‖a‖_v = exp(−[k(v) : k]·ord_v(a)). The constant field k is kept fixed under extension of K. h is independent of homogeneous coordinates and of the choice of K′.
hypotheses: K/k of transcendence degree one; k not necessarily algebraically closed.
proofSteps: Product formula on the regular projective curve of K′ (degrees of principal divisors vanish, weighted by [k(v) : k]) gives independence of coordinates.
Dividing by [K′ : K] gives independence of K′ (sum over places above v of e·f equals the degree).
Compare with the parent’s heights over polarized function fields (RP.0): for k algebraically closed the weights are 1 and the two agree.

sources.match: Defines the projective height over a function field of one variable, with residue-degree weights over a fixed constant field and division by the extension degree, and records its independence of choices.

acceptance: For K = k(t), h([1 : t]) = 1 (one pole of order 1 at infinity, residue degree 1).
For k = ℝ, K = ℝ(t) and x = [1 : 1/(t² + 1)], h(x) = 2: the place t² + 1 has residue degree 2 over ℝ.
h([1 : c]) = 0 for c ∈ k; a height without residue weights would give the wrong value when k is not algebraically closed (e.g. [1 : 1/(t² + 1)] over ℝ(t) would get 1).

uses.how: heights over function fields are normalized this way, uniformly in k
deĝ(M̄|_y) uses the same weights

nodes.title: Isotrivial curve–line-bundle pairs
nodes.statement: Fix a function field K of one variable over k and an embedding k̄ → K̄. A pair (C, α) over K̄, with C a smooth projective curve of genus g > 1 and α a line bundle of degree d on C, is isotrivial (over k) if it is isomorphic to the scalar extension of a pair (C₀, α₀) over k̄; otherwise it is non-isotrivial. Triples (C, η, α) with a full level-N structure η (N ≥ 3 prime to char k) are defined isotrivial in the same way.
hypotheses: K/k of transcendence degree one; g > 1.
proofSteps: A predicate on isomorphism classes of pairs over K̄ relative to the fixed embedding of k̄.

sources.match: Defines isotriviality of curves with line bundles (and with level structure) over function fields, noting that the curve alone may be constant while the pair is not.

acceptance: Let C₀/k be smooth projective of genus >1 and K=k(C₀). On the constant curve C=C₀×_k K̄ take α=O(x) for its generic K-point x. Then C is isotrivial and the pair (C,α) is non-isotrivial.
C₀ ⊗ K̄ with α = α₀ ⊗ K̄ is isotrivial.
The notion is only for function fields: over a number field there is no constant field to compare with, and Yuan’s theorem needs no such hypothesis there.

uses.how: the uniform bound over function fields assumes (C_{K̄}, α) non-isotrivial
non-isotriviality can be tested with level structure or after the canonical shift

nodes.title: Isotriviality via level structure, canonical shift and the moduli point (Yuan Lemma 4.8)
nodes.statement: Let K/k be a function field of one variable, k̄ ⊆ K̄ fixed, and (C, η, α) over K̄ of genus g > 1, full level N ≥ 3 prime to char k, deg α = d. (a) (C, η, α) is isotrivial iff (C, α) is isotrivial. (b) (C, η, α) descends to k̄ iff (C, η, (2g − 2)α − d·ω_C) does. (c) The triple corresponding to a point of Pic^d_{𝒞/M_{g,N}}(K̄) is isotrivial iff that point comes from Pic^d_{𝒞/M_{g,N}}(k̄), equivalently its image in the k-scheme Pic^d_{𝒞/M_{g,N}} is a closed point. Geometric torsion points, including p-primary ones, are unchanged under algebraically closed constant extension.
hypotheses: N ≥ 3 prime to char k; g > 1.
proofSteps: (a) Rigidity of level structures (StableReductionPartII MC.4): a level-N structure on an isotrivial curve is defined over k̄ after the identification, since the level-N torsion of a constant Jacobian is constant.

(b) α ↦ (2g − 2)α − dω_C is a finite map on Pic^d with finite fibres (translates by (2g − 2)-torsion), and torsion of a constant Jacobian is constant, including p-primary torsion over algebraically closed k̄.
(c) The fine moduli space M_{g,N} and its relative Picard scheme represent triples (MC.7); a K̄-point comes from k̄ iff it factors through the closed points of the k-scheme.

sources.locator: Lemma 4.8, p. 74, and §4.3.2, p. 75 (author manuscript 21 August 2024)
sources.match: Shows that non-isotriviality is unaffected by adding level structure and by the canonical shift, and identifies isotrivial triples with constant points of the relative Picard scheme over the fine moduli space.

acceptance: The full level structure supplies a fine moduli space with a universal curve and relative Picard scheme representing triples. Without it that representability argument is unavailable; this alone does not disprove the corresponding criterion on geometric isomorphism classes.
The function μ_N in clause (3) of the triple definition is over F = k̄ (source issue E19 of the Yuan extraction).

nodes.title: Small points over the universal shift by noetherian induction (Yuan §4.4.1)
nodes.statement: Work over a field with a chosen primitive N-th root of unity and N invertible, or over B=Spec ℤ[1/N,ζ_N], N ≥ 3. Let S = M_{g,N} be the fine symplectic-level moduli scheme over this base of smooth genus-g > 1 curves with full level-N structure and π : X → S its universal curve (more generally, S quasi-finite over M_g, so that every closed subvariety of S has generically finite moduli map). With J = Pic⁰_{X/S}, Θ̄ its canonical nef symmetric twice-theta adelic bundle, X_J = J ×_S X, J_J = J ×_S J, q₁ : X_J → J, τ(y, x) = (y, y + (2g − 2)x − ω) and L̄ = τ^*p₂^*Θ̄: for every adelic M̄ on J (over ℤ in the arithmetic case) there are c₁, c₂ > 0 with #{z ∈ X_J(K̄) : q₁(z) = y, h_{L̄}(z) ≤ c₁h_{M̄}(y)} ≤ c₂ for all y ∈ J(K̄) over number fields, and the analogous bound with deĝ(M̄|_y) for non-isotrivial function-field points.
hypotheses: S = M_{g,N} with its universal curve, or S quasi-finite over M_g; g > 1.
proofSteps: L̄ is potentially big on X_J/J (AH.12, theta potential bigness part (3)); the small-points bound gives the claim on a dense open U ⊆ J.

For every irreducible closed Y ⊆ J ∖ U, the restriction of L̄ to X_Y is potentially big over Y (part (4), whose hypothesis is that the image T of Y in S has generically finite moduli map — automatic for S quasi-finite over M_g, which is why S is the fine moduli space — with dim T for dim S as in source issue E16); apply the bound on a dense open of Y.
Noetherian induction on closed subsets of J terminates after finitely many steps; normalize subvarieties where the bound needs normal bases.

Over B=Spec ℤ[1/N,ζ_N], Theorem 4.10 applies to the horizontal integral strata after normalization. Vertical strata are varieties over finite fields and require the geometric small-points theorem 4.2(2); a vertical component is not flat over ℤ. The all-characteristic bookkeeping is kept separate in UB.11/characteristic-uniformity.

sources.match: Over the fine moduli space M_{g,N} and its universal curve, applies the small-points bound to the universal shift family on a dense open of J, then to every closed subvariety by potential bigness of the restriction (whose hypothesis is a generically finite moduli map on the image in S), terminating by dimension.

acceptance: The constants depend on the family X → S and on M̄ only.
Without part (4) of theta potential bigness the induction cannot leave the generic open set.

nodes.title: Heights on the universal shift and the moduli height (Yuan §4.4.1)
nodes.statement: In the setting of the noetherian induction bound over a number field, for z = (y, x) ∈ X_J(K̄) above s ∈ S(K̄): h_{L̄}(z) = 2ĥ((2g − 2)x − (ω_{X_s} − y)). For M̄ = Θ̄ + π_J^*λ̄_S + O(c), with λ̄_S the adelic Hodge bundle of X → S, h_{M̄}(y) = 2ĥ(y) + h_Fal(X_s) + c. Bost’s lower bound for the Faltings height then gives h_{M̄}(y) ≥ c₃(max{h_Fal(X_s), 1} + ĥ(y)) for a suitable c.
hypotheses: number-field normalization; s ∈ S(K̄).
proofSteps: Projection formula for τ₁ = p₂ ∘ τ : X_J → J, with τ₁(y, x) the class of y + (2g − 2)x − ω on X_s: h_{L̄}(z) = h_Θ(τ₁(z)) = 2ĥ(τ₁(z)), and [−1] symmetry of ĥ.
h_{Θ̄}(y) = 2ĥ(y), h_{λ̄_S}(s) = h_Fal(X_s) (AH.5, adelic Hodge bundle computes the Faltings height), and O(c) has height c.

Bost’s bound h_Fal ≥ −C(g) (AH.13, in the Faltings normalization; the constant printed by Yuan uses Deligne’s normalization, an erratum recorded by the Arakelov Part II plan): with c = C(g) + 1, h_{M̄}(y) = 2ĥ(y) + h_Fal(X_s) + c ≥ ĥ(y) + max{h_Fal(X_s), 1}, so c₃ = 1 works.

sources.match: Computes the heights of the theta pullback along the universal shift and of the auxiliary bundle built from the twice-theta bundle and the Hodge bundle, and uses Bost’s lower bound for the Faltings height.

acceptance: For y = ω − (2g − 2)α with α of degree 1, (2g − 2)x − (ω − y) = (2g − 2)(x − α), so the identity converts the claim into a bound for ĥ(x − α).
The shift y ↦ ω − (2g − 2)α is surjective on degree-0 classes after extending K, which is why α may be any class in Pic¹(C_{K̄}).

nodes.title: Moduli height domination over function fields (Yuan §4.4.2)
nodes.statement: Over a field k, in the setting of the noetherian induction bound, take M̄ = Θ̄ + π_J^*λ̄_{S̄} + N with N ample on a projective compactification of J. For every point y ∈ J of dimension one with image s ∈ S, deĝ(M̄|_y) ≥ 2ĥ(y) + h_Fal(X_{s, k(y)}) + 1, the last term coming from the positive integral degree of N on the closure of y.
hypotheses: k a field; y a dimension-one point of J.
proofSteps: Degrees are additive: deĝ(Θ̄|_y) = 2ĥ(y) in the normalization over k(y)/k, deĝ(λ̄|_y) = h_Fal(X_s) for the function-field Faltings height (AH.13) with the Hodge bundle on the stable compactification.
N is ample on a projective model, so its degree on the closure of y is a positive integer, at least 1.

sources.match: Bounds the degree of the auxiliary adelic line bundle on a one-dimensional point from below by the Néron–Tate height, the Faltings height of the fibre and 1.

acceptance: The constant 1 replaces Bost’s bound: over function fields h_Fal ≥ 0 (AH.13).
For isotrivial points the degree of N on the (zero-dimensional) closure is not defined; only dimension-one points are considered.

nodes.title: Uniformity of the constants across all global fields (Yuan §4.4.3)
nodes.statement: For each g > 1 the constants of the uniform small-points bound for genus-g curves can be chosen depending only on g, simultaneously for all number fields and all function fields of one variable over all fields k of all characteristics.
proofSteps: Over S=M_{g,N} over B=Spec ℤ[1/N,ζ_N], apply the integral small-points bound to q₁:X_J→J, with L̄=τ^*Θ̄_J and M̄=Θ̄+π_J^*λ̄_S+N̄. Its initial exceptional locus is a proper closed subset of J, the actual parameter space for y; it is not automatically a subset of S.

Apply the integral bound successively to horizontal components of the exceptional locus in J, using theta potential bigness after restriction and normalization. Dimension drops over ℚ, leaving a vertical closed subset of J with image in finitely many characteristics. This needs the restricted-family input; projecting one initial exceptional locus to S would not suffice.

For each remaining prime p (including primes dividing N), choose N″≥3 prime to p and run the geometric small-points theorem 4.2(2) on the universal shift over a fixed symplectic component of M_{g,N″} after adjoining ζ_{N″} to 𝔽_p, with noetherian induction on its Jacobian. The required uniform statement across constant-field extensions must be justified in this geometric setting; Yuan omits these details and the gap remains. It is not an application of Theorem 4.10 to a base flat over ℤ.
Number fields are covered by the arithmetic case; take the extrema of the finitely many constants (source issue E15 of the Yuan extraction corrects the cross-references to Theorem 4.7).

The cyclotomic base is finite flat over ℤ[1/N]. Geometric height normalization is invariant under finite extension of the function field; arithmetic heights are absolute. Thus adjoining level roots does not introduce constants depending on the input field.

sources.match: Works over the full-level moduli space over ℤ[1/N], applies the integral small-points bound and induction to remove the exceptional locus over ℚ, and treats the finitely many remaining characteristics over separate prime-to-p levels over 𝔽_p, taking extrema of finitely many constants; the details for the finitely many characteristics are omitted in the source.

acceptance: The level N is fixed; changing it only changes finitely many characteristics.
Uniformity over k is genuine: the constants do not depend on the constant field, which may be non-algebraically closed.

nodes.title: The uniform Bogomolov-type theorem for curves (Yuan Theorem 1.1)
nodes.statement: For each integer g > 1 there are c₁(g), c₂(g) > 0, valid simultaneously for all number fields and all function fields of one variable over any field k, in every characteristic, such that: for every smooth projective geometrically integral curve C of genus g over K and every α ∈ Pic(C_{K̄}) of degree 1, assuming in the function-field case that (C_{K̄}, α) is non-isotrivial over k, #{x ∈ C(K̄) : ĥ(x − α) ≤ c₁(max{h_Fal(C), 1} + ĥ((2g − 2)α − ω_{C/K}))} ≤ c₂. Here ĥ is half the canonical height of the symmetric twice-theta bundle, normalized absolutely over ℚ for number fields and over K/k (fixed k) for function fields.
hypotheses: g > 1; K a number field or a function field of one variable over k; (C_{K̄}, α) non-isotrivial in the function-field case.
proofSteps: Choose a full level N and pass to a finite extension of K over which the level structure is defined (heights are invariant).

Number fields: the noetherian induction bound for the universal family with M̄ = Θ̄ + π_J^*λ̄_S + O(c), the shifted height identity, and y = ω − (2g − 2)α give #{x : (2g − 2)²ĥ(x − α) ≤ c₁c₃(max{h_Fal, 1} + ĥ(ω − (2g − 2)α))} ≤ c₂.
Function fields: the same with the geometric moduli domination and Lemma 4.8 to translate non-isotriviality of the moduli point; replace h_Fal + 1 by max{h_Fal, 1} using h_Fal ≥ 0.
Uniformity in K across characteristics: the characteristic-uniformity theorem.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.1, p. 5, and Theorem 4.7, p. 70; proof §4.4, pp. 76–84 (author manuscript 21 August 2024)
sources.match: States the uniform bound for points of small height relative to a degree-one class, strengthening the new gap principle by the extra term ĥ((2g − 2)α − ω), allowing α ∈ Pic¹ and covering global fields of all characteristics with uniform constants; the proof rests on bigness of the admissible canonical bundle on the universal curve.

acceptance: For α = y ∈ C(K̄) over a number field, dropping the non-negative term ĥ((2g − 2)α − ω) recovers the new gap principle for curves.
The non-isotriviality hypothesis is on the pair: for a constant curve and a constant α there are infinitely many points of height 0.
Taking the threshold term only (c₁ max{h_Fal, 1}) and Γ = torsion gives uniform Manin–Mumford for curves over global fields of every characteristic (for non-isotrivial pairs).

nodes.title: Bielliptic genus-two curves as lifts of the diagonal (DKY Proposition 9.1)
nodes.statement: Every smooth genus-2 curve X over ℂ admitting a degree-2 map to an elliptic curve has a model y² = x⁶ − s₁x⁴ + s₂x² − 1 and is the normalization of the lift of the diagonal D ⊆ ℙ¹ × ℙ¹ under π₁ × π₂, for elliptic curves E₁, E₂ with standard projections π_i satisfying |π₁(E₁[2]) ∩ π₂(E₂[2])| = 3, the group laws taken with origins O_i over a common branch value r. There are a Weierstrass point Q of X and an isogeny Φ : J(X) → E₁ × E₂ of degree 4 with Φ(j_Q(X)) = (π₁ × π₂)^{-1}(D); the non-zero elements of ker Φ are the differences of the two Weierstrass points over each common branch value.
hypotheses: X smooth genus 2 over ℂ with a degree-2 map to an elliptic curve.
proofSteps: The Jacobi model of bielliptic genus-two curves is cited from Shaska–Völklein and Jacobi (not proved here); the two involutions (x, y) ↦ (−x, ±y) give quotients E₁, E₂.

The quotient maps combine to J(X) → E₁ × E₂ with kernel the 2-torsion classes listed; the image of the Abel–Jacobi curve based at a Weierstrass point Q over the common branch value r is the preimage of the diagonal (McMullen, Theorem 4.10, as DKY use it).

sources.locator: §§9.1–9.2, Proposition 9.1 and proof, pp. 45–47 (arXiv v2); published version pp. 994–996
sources.match: Represents every bielliptic genus-two curve through the diagonal of the product of the two elliptic quotients with three common branch values, giving a degree-four isogeny of the Jacobian onto E₁ × E₂ carrying the Abel–Jacobi curve to the lift of the diagonal.

Represents every bielliptic genus-two curve through the diagonal of the product of the two elliptic quotients with three common branch values, giving a degree-four isogeny of the Jacobian onto E₁ × E₂ carrying the Abel–Jacobi curve to the lift of the diagonal.

acceptance: The bielliptic locus in M₂ is a surface (Jacobians with real multiplication by the order of discriminant 4).
Exactly three common branch values occur; two would not give a degree-4 isogeny of this shape.

nodes.title: Uniform Manin–Mumford for bielliptic genus-two curves (DKY Theorem 1.1)
nodes.statement: There is a uniform B such that |j_P(X) ∩ J(X)_tors| ≤ B for every smooth bielliptic genus-2 curve X over ℂ and every Weierstrass point P of X, where j_P is the Abel–Jacobi embedding based at P.
hypotheses: X bielliptic of genus 2 over ℂ; P a Weierstrass point.
proofSteps: A common x-coordinate has at most four lifts to E₁×E₂, and each point has at most four preimages under the degree-four isogeny Φ. Thus at most sixteen points of j_Q(X) lie above each common coordinate.
The common torsion images are uniformly bounded (ArithmeticDynamics DY.6, the three-common-branch-values bound).
Any other Weierstrass point P differs from Q by a 2-torsion class, so j_P(X) is a 2-torsion translate of j_Q(X) and has the same number of torsion points.
Consistency: the uniform Manin–Mumford theorem for curves gives the same conclusion with B = c(2); DKY’s proof is the independent dynamical one.

sources.match: Bounds the torsion points on the Abel–Jacobi image of a bielliptic genus-two curve by 16 times the number of common torsion images of the two elliptic quotients, which is uniformly bounded, and passes between Weierstrass base points by 2-torsion translation.

Bounds the torsion points on the Abel–Jacobi image of a bielliptic genus-two curve by 16 times the number of common torsion images of the two elliptic quotients, which is uniformly bounded, and passes between Weierstrass base points by 2-torsion translation.

acceptance: Stoll’s curve y² = x⁶ + 130x³ + 13, which is bielliptic, has 34 torsion points on its Weierstrass Abel–Jacobi image, so B ≥ 34.
The bound is not explicit in DKY (Remark 1.2).

nodes.title: Uniform Bogomolov for bielliptic genus-two curves (DKY Theorem 1.9; Theorem 1.10 of the published version)
nodes.statement: There are B and b > 0 such that |{x ∈ j_P(X)(ℚ̄) : ĥ_{L_X}(x) ≤ b}| ≤ B for every smooth genus-2 curve X over ℚ̄ with a degree-2 map to an elliptic curve and every Weierstrass point P, where L_X = Φ^*L_D for the isogeny Φ : J(X) → E₁ × E₂ of the diagonal-lift proposition and D = {O₁} × E₂ + E₁ × {O₂}.
hypotheses: X bielliptic of genus 2 over ℚ̄; P Weierstrass.
proofSteps: Functoriality: ĥ_{L_X} = ½(ĥ_{t₁} ∘ π ∘ Φ₁ + ĥ_{t₂} ∘ π ∘ Φ₂), with Lattès heights of the two elliptic quotients (ArithmeticDynamics DY.6).

A point of j_Q(X) of small ĥ_{L_X} maps to a point x of ℙ¹ with ĥ_{t₁}(x) + ĥ_{t₂}(x) small; the uniform joint small-points bound (DKY Theorem 8.1, DY.6) bounds such x, each with at most 16 preimages.

For any Weierstrass P, the class P−Q is 2-torsion. Translation by torsion leaves the quadratic canonical height for the same symmetric L_X exactly unchanged. The bijection j_Q(X)→j_P(X) therefore preserves the small-point count and supplies the missing base-point step in the printed proof (DKY E8).

sources.locator: Theorem 1.9, p. 5; proof §9.4, p. 47 (arXiv v2); published version Theorem 1.10, p. 953, proof §9.4, p. 997
sources.match: Proves uniform Bogomolov for the Abel–Jacobi images of bielliptic genus-two curves from the uniform bound on joint small points of two Lattès maps, writing the height for the pulled-back divisor as half the sum of the Lattès heights.

Proves uniform Bogomolov for the Abel–Jacobi images of bielliptic genus-two curves from the uniform bound on joint small points of two Lattès maps, writing the height for the pulled-back divisor as half the sum of the Lattès heights.

acceptance: A special case of the uniform Bogomolov theorem (Gao–Ge–Kühne Theorem 1.3) for X = j_P(X) in J(X) with the polarization L_X.
The threshold b is absolute, not scaled by the Faltings height.

nodes.title: No uniform bound on torsion orders (DKY Proposition 9.2 of the published version)
nodes.statement: For every N > 0 there are a bielliptic genus-2 curve X over ℚ̄ and a Weierstrass point P ∈ X such that j_P(X) ∩ J(X)_tors contains a point of order ≥ N.
proofSteps: Choose Legendre parameters t₁ ≠ t₂ with a common x-coordinate whose points have order ≥ N on both curves (DY.6, unbounded orders of common torsion images).

By the diagonal-lift proposition this pair lies under a point w of j_Q(X) for the bielliptic curve with these quotients; the finite kernel of Φ makes w torsion of order at least the order of its image, so ≥ N.

sources.locator: Proposition 9.2 and proof, §9.5, p. 997; Proposition 8.3, p. 994
sources.match: Shows that the torsion points on the Abel–Jacobi images can have arbitrarily large order, so only their number is uniformly bounded.

acceptance: Contrast with uniform Manin–Mumford: the number of torsion points is bounded, their orders are not.
Kühne makes the same remark for general curves (Theorem 2 and the comment after it).

gaps.title: Rémond’s Décompte read only through Gao–Ge–Kühne Appendix A
gaps.detail: Rémond, Décompte dans une conjecture de Lang (Invent. Math. 142 (2000), Propositions 3.3–3.4, Lemma 3.1, Lemme 6.1) could not be obtained; its statements are taken from GGK Appendix A, which restates them with n = deg_L A/g! − 1. Rémond’s Vojta paper (Ann. SNS Pisa 2000, Théorème 1.1) was read and agrees with GGK Theorem A.1. The proofs (explicit Mumford inequality, isolated fibres, height of X) are Rémond’s quantitative versions of the parent’s Vojta method and need their own lemma-level plan. In particular, UB.5/subvariety-height-removal needs arithmetic interpolation, not a Bézout argument using hypersurfaces containing X. Supply that estimate with its finite nonempty-set and positive-dimension hypotheses.

gaps.title: Chow-form heights compared with arithmetic-intersection heights
gaps.detail: The comparison between the Weil height of the Chow form and the Bost–Gillet–Soulé height of a cycle (Philippon, Math. Ann. 289 (1991); Bost–Gillet–Soulé, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 7 (1994)) was not read; the papers routed here only fix some height of cycles. The parent’s projective cycle heights (RP.5) plan the coefficient-height comparison it rests on.

gaps.title: Masser’s 1989 specialization theorem not read
gaps.detail: Masser, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 311 (1989), Main Theorem and Scholium 1 (Zariski density of specializations injective on a finitely generated group of sections) could not be downloaded and is taken as GGK cite it; Masser 1996 (endomorphism rings) was read. The precise missing step is simultaneous density of subgroup-injective and endomorphism-preserving fibres via a common quantitative exceptional-set bound. Separate Zariski-density assertions cannot be intersected to prove it.

gaps.title: Yamaki’s reduction theorem cited, not planned
gaps.detail: Yamaki, J. reine angew. Math. 2018, Theorem 1.5 (statement checked against arXiv 1405.0896v5), reducing the geometric Bogomolov conjecture to the nowhere degenerate trace-free part, rests on Gubler’s tropical equidistribution at places of bad reduction; no roadmap of the atlas plans it. It is an input theorem here.

gaps.title: Positive-characteristic step of Yuan §4.4.3 omitted in the source
gaps.detail: The initial exceptional locus lies in J, not S. Induct on its horizontal components using theta potential bigness after restriction; after normalization only finitely many vertical characteristics remain. For these use Theorem 4.2(2) over a prime-to-p symplectic-level component over 𝔽_p with the level roots adjoined. Theorem 4.10 cannot be applied directly to a vertical base, which is not flat over ℤ. A proof uniform in all constant-field extensions is still needed; the source omits it on p. 84.

gaps.title: Jacobi model of bielliptic genus-two curves cited
gaps.detail: DeMarco–Krieger–Ye cite the model y² = x⁶ − s₁x⁴ + s₂x² − 1 from Shaska–Völklein and Jacobi and McMullen’s Theorem 4.10; neither is planned in the atlas.

gaps.title: Controlled embedding constants for general polarization types
gaps.detail: DGH (8.4), (8.7) bounds c_NT and a chosen addition-polynomial height for its fixed principally polarized universal-family embeddings. GGK §7.1 invokes the extension to arbitrary fixed polarization degree, citing David–Philippon (6.41). That direct source and the corresponding theta-embedding construction have not been checked here. The general bound must be established before substituting h_Fal into the raw Rémond inequalities. Arbitrary projective coordinate changes cannot satisfy a moduli-only bound.

restructure.detail: The design job received twelve paper routes in five independent directions of the parent. Seven (Yuan 2026, Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger 2021, DeMarco–Krieger–Ye 2020, Gao–Habegger 2019, Xie–Yuan 2022, DeMarco–Mavraki–Ye 2026, Gao–Ge–Kühne 2026) form the uniformity programme for small points and Mordell–Lang, planned here. The other five share no definitions with it: Browning–Le Boudec–Sawin 2023 (Hasse principle for random Fano hypersurfaces; route HeightsRationalPointsPartIIRandomFano), Skorobogatov–Sofos 2023 (Schinzel’s hypothesis on average and random norm/conic fibrations; HeightsRationalPointsPartIIRandomFibrations), Harpaz–Wittenberg 2023 and the Massey route of Harpaz–Wittenberg 2020 (Massey vanishing over number fields and homogeneous spaces with supersolvable stabilizers; HeightsRationalPointsPartIIHomogeneousMassey), and the zero-cycle route of Harpaz–Wittenberg 2020 (Theorem A; HeightsRationalPointsPartIIZeroCycles).
restructure.proposal: Keep HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructionsPartII as “Heights, rational points and obstructions, Part II: uniform Bogomolov and uniform Mordell–Lang” (stages UB.0–UB.12). Give each of the four other route ids its own design job, each a Part II of HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions with its paper routes as brief: RandomFano (BLBS23), RandomFibrations (SS23, importing ArithmeticStatisticsPartIISchinzelAverages), HomogeneousMassey (HW23 + HW20 Theorem 6.6 foundation, importing ProfiniteCohomologyPartIIMasseyGalois) and ZeroCycles (HW20 Theorem A). The HW20 fibration and descent foundation shared by the last two is owned by HomogeneousMassey, designed first; ZeroCycles imports it.

restructure.detail: The height inequality for non-degenerate subvarieties appears twice: ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeightsPartII AH.5/non-degenerate-height-inequality plans the Yuan–Zhang version for polarized dynamical systems over number fields (adelic volumes), and UB.2/height-inequality plans Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger’s Theorem B.1 for abelian schemes with the geometric proof (Betti form, graph construction, Siu).
